title: Bitcoin Packs 11,255 Transactions Into a Single Block, Nears Record
summary: Bitcoin’s blockchain came within striking distance of an 11-year-old transaction record on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, when a single block processed 11,255 transactions, the second-highest total in network history, amid a year already producing extraordinary daily transaction counts. Bitcoin’s 2015 Tran...
content:
Bitcoin’s blockchain came within striking distance of an 11-year-old transaction record on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, when a single block processed 11,255 transactions, the second-highest total in network history, amid a year already producing extraordinary daily transaction counts.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin’s 2015 transaction record emerged from an unusual cleanup of spam-related outputs, while today’s contenders rely on entirely different techniques.
  • Bitcoin’s exceptionally dense blocks demonstrate how specialized minting operations can inflate transaction counts without generating substantial fees or transferring significant value.
  • Modern transaction engineering is allowing miners to approach historical records without changing the network’s 4 million weight-unit limit.

Bitcoin’s 2015 Transaction Record Faces Its Closest Challenger in 11 Years

Bitcoin’s transaction history is getting a serious workout in 2026, and the latest development has brought a seemingly untouchable record back into focus. Block 974961, mined by Antpool on Nov. 7, contained an astonishing 11,255 transactions, placing it just 984 transactions behind the all-time record established in August 2015.

The latest milestone follows another extraordinary block discovered three days earlier. On Nov. 4, Mempool.space developer Mononaut highlighted the network’s unusually dense transaction activity in a post on X, stating:

“Block 974557 contained 10,573 transactions, the second highest figure of all time!”

That distinction lasted only three days. On Nov. 7, Mononaut returned to X with another observation, this time documenting an even larger collection of transactions squeezed into a single Bitcoin block. The Mempool.space programmer said:

“New #2 record: 11,255. We’re rapidly closing in on the all-time high of 12,239 transactions from block 367853”

The new runner-up, block 974961, was mined at 18:24:12 UTC and measured approximately 1.1 megabytes (MB), according to blockchain data. Despite accommodating more than 11,000 transactions, it consumed 3,993,844 weight units, equivalent to roughly 99.85% of Bitcoin’s maximum block weight.

Even more curious was the economics behind the achievement. The block collected approximately 0.002405 BTC in transaction fees, a negligible addition to the standard 3.125 BTC block subsidy. Its 11,794 inputs and 23,122 outputs reflected an unusually large collection of compact transactions rather than a procession of conventional, high-value bitcoin transfers.

In other words, Bitcoin managed to accommodate an extraordinary number of transactions without requiring an equally extraordinary amount of block space or fee expenditure.

Why Does a Bitcoin Block From 2015 Still Hold the Record?

To appreciate the significance of November’s achievement, one must revisit Aug. 1, 2015, when mining pool F2pool produced block 367853. That block contained 12,239 transactions, a record that has survived more than 11 years of technological changes, network upgrades, and fluctuating transaction demand.

Unlike today’s Bitcoin blocks, which operate under a 4 million weight-unit limit, the 2015 block was constrained by the original 1 MB size ceiling. F2pool nevertheless managed to pack 12,239 transactions into approximately 999.96 kilobytes, an exceptional feat under the network’s earlier architecture.

The circumstances were hardly ordinary. Bitcoin was enduring a period of what some called spam attacks or deliberate network stress tests, including reported campaigns that generated enormous quantities of tiny, low-value transaction outputs.

The activity also brought renewed attention to Bitcoin’s unspent transaction output (UTXO) set, which became another point of discussion in the broader debate over network efficiency, scalability, and block size limits.

A UTXO represents bitcoin received through a previous transaction that remains available to spend. Every Bitcoin full node must maintain information about these unspent outputs to determine whether subsequent transactions are valid and whether the same coins are being spent twice.

During the 2015 UTXO waves, enormous quantities of dust outputs accumulated across the network. F2pool subsequently undertook cleanup efforts that consolidated these outputs, reducing the number of individual entries nodes needed to track.

Block 367853 emerged from that unusual episode. Rather than containing thousands of ordinary financial transactions, it included exceptionally small, nonstandard transactions, some measuring approximately 62 bytes, allowing the miner to maximize the number of transactions inside the available space.

F2pool also mined block 367851 that day, containing 9,647 transactions. Together, these blocks demonstrated how miners could construct unusually dense blocks using transactions that would not ordinarily propagate through standard network relay channels.

The 2015 record was therefore a product of specialized transaction engineering and network housekeeping, not simply overwhelming consumer demand for bitcoin payments.

How Segwit and Runes Are Pushing Bitcoin’s Transaction Limits

Fast-forward to 2026, and the mechanics behind Bitcoin’s densely packed blocks look considerably different. Much of the recent activity involves highly compact transactions associated with the Runes protocol, particularly minting activity involving UNCOMMON•GOODS, the first rune introduced around Bitcoin’s fourth halving in April 2024.

These transactions can use lightweight pay-to-anchor (P2A) outputs and carefully optimized structures, sometimes measuring approximately 80 to 100 virtual bytes. Their modest size allows miners to fit thousands more transactions into a block than would be possible using larger, conventional transaction formats.

Another important ingredient is Segregated Witness (Segwit), Bitcoin’s August 2017 upgrade that separated transaction signature data from the information used to calculate traditional transaction identifiers. Segwit introduced block weight, allowing witness data to count less heavily toward Bitcoin’s capacity limit.

The distinction matters because Bitcoin’s transaction capacity cannot be measured simply by counting bytes. Two blocks consuming comparable weight can contain dramatically different transaction totals depending on their contents.

That helps explain why block 974961 could accommodate 11,255 transactions while collecting virtually nothing in fees. The record-setting count reflects transaction efficiency and specialized protocol activity, not necessarily an equivalent increase in economic demand.

The development also raises an important distinction between transaction throughput and actual monetary settlement. A blockchain processing thousands of small token-related operations is not necessarily transferring more bitcoin value than one processing substantially fewer, larger financial transactions.

Seven of Bitcoin’s 10 Busiest Transaction Days Occurred in 2026

The extraordinary block counts are not isolated curiosities. Bitcoin’s daily transaction records tell a similarly compelling story, with seven of the ten busiest days in the network’s history occurring during 2026.

The all-time daily record remains April 23, 2024, when Bitcoin processed 927,010 transactions shortly after the fourth halving and the introduction of Runes. However, Oct. 23, 2026, came exceptionally close, recording 913,196 transactions, just 13,814 short of the historic peak.

RankDateBitcoin Transactions per Day
1Apr. 23, 2024927,010
2Oct. 23, 2026913,196
3Sept. 8, 2024910,083
4Oct. 5, 2026904,518
5July 19, 2026898,862

October also delivered another major milestone on Oct. 5, when the network processed 904,518 transactions. Additional entries from July, August, September and June demonstrate that 2026’s elevated activity extended across multiple months rather than originating from one isolated episode.

Yet November has introduced an intriguing contradiction.

During the first seven days of the month, the Bitcoin protocol averaged approximately 534,200 transactions daily, roughly 25% below October’s average of 710,400. On Nov. 2, daily activity fell to 381,886 transactions, the lowest reading since March 17.

The slowdown coincided with considerable turbulence across cryptocurrency markets following the late-October Binance security breach and subsequent declines in bitcoin’s market price.

Nevertheless, the network produced its second-largest transaction block on Nov. 7, when daily activity recovered to 591,830 transactions.

This contrast illustrates why individual block records and daily transaction totals should be interpreted separately. A miner can assemble an exceptionally dense block containing specialized transactions even when overall network activity is running below its recent averages.

Will Bitcoin Finally Break Its 12,239-Transaction Record?

The remaining distance between Bitcoin’s newest milestone and its historic record is surprisingly narrow. Another 985 transactions beyond November’s second-place block would establish a new all-time high.

Whether that happens depends less on conventional bitcoin payment demand than on the continued production of exceptionally compact transactions and miners’ willingness to include them.

The broader picture is equally revealing. Bitcoin’s busiest transaction days increasingly reflect specialized blockchain applications, while traditional monetary activity represents only one component of total network usage.

For now, the 2015 record remains intact, but its longevity no longer makes it appear untouchable. Eleven years after F2pool filled a block with thousands of unconventional transactions, modern miners are approaching the same territory through entirely different technical methods. The contest demonstrates that Bitcoin’s transaction count is as much a function of how transactions are constructed as how frequently the network is used.

title: FinCEN Withdraws Proposed Crypto Travel Rule Expansion in Separate November Move
summary: FinCEN and the Federal Reserve are withdrawing a proposed expansion of US recordkeeping and Travel Rule requirements that would have covered certain…
content:
TL;DR: FinCEN and the Federal Reserve are withdrawing a proposed expansion of US recordkeeping and Travel Rule requirements that would have covered certain convertible virtual currency transfers and lowered a cross-border transfer threshold. The withdrawal removes a proposal; it does not cancel existing anti-money-laundering obligations.

Two announcements issued by the same US agency on November 6 point in different regulatory directions. While FinCEN imposed a targeted financial restriction on MEXC Global, it also announced that it was withdrawing a previously proposed update to the Recordkeeping and Travel Rule for funds transfers.

According to FinCEN’s release, the proposal would have amended requirements relating to convertible virtual currencies and certain digital assets. It would also have lowered a threshold for transfers beginning or ending outside the United States. The Federal Reserve Board joined the withdrawal.

A withdrawn proposal is not a repeal of the Travel Rule

This distinction is central to understanding the announcement. A proposal describes changes regulators are considering. Withdrawing it means those proposed changes will not proceed through that rulemaking in their existing form. It does not mean every reporting, customer-identification or information-sharing requirement currently applying to financial institutions has disappeared.

The Travel Rule generally addresses information that financial institutions must collect or transmit when handling covered transfers. In the digital asset industry, implementation raises difficult questions about service-provider identities, unhosted wallets and transfers that cross multiple systems. A proposed amendment can change where those obligations attach or what thresholds apply, but it cannot be read as the whole compliance framework.

FinCEN explicitly frames this action as the withdrawal of a notice of proposed rulemaking. Companies should therefore update regulatory trackers and comment schedules without treating it as permission to suspend controls that already exist under separate law.

Why the decision matters for crypto payments

Rules governing transfer information affect the customer experience as well as the institution behind it. More extensive data-collection requirements can add operational cost, create friction during international payments and complicate relationships between banks and crypto businesses. Supporters of stricter rules argue that traceability is needed to investigate laundering and sanctions evasion; opponents can point to privacy, proportionality and practical implementation burdens.

The November announcement does not settle that debate. It signals that the agencies have chosen not to move ahead with this particular expansion. A future rulemaking or different targeted action remains possible, and the exact scope of any later proposal cannot be inferred now.

That sits beside FinCEN’s much harder action against MEXC: the agency can withdraw a broad proposal while using existing powers against entities it believes pose specific risks. The two decisions are not mutually exclusive.

What compliance teams should watch next

Banks, exchanges and payment providers should review the published withdrawal documents, identify which previously planned systems changes relied on the abandoned proposal, and keep existing transfer-screening arrangements in place unless their legal teams determine otherwise. Cross-border businesses should pay particular attention to the difference between US requirements and rules in the jurisdictions where counterparties operate.

For broader context, NewsBTC has followed how regulatory changes alter stablecoin access in Europe. This is another reminder that regulation often changes the infrastructure customers use without changing the underlying technology of a token.

The next useful development would be a clear timetable for any replacement rule, or fresh agency guidance on affected transfers. Until then, the precise conclusion is modest but important: a proposed reporting expansion has been withdrawn, while the underlying AML regime continues.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Lightning Network Security Scare Forces LNbits Servers Offline
summary: LNbits, the open-source Lightning Network wallet and payments platform, issued an emergency shutdown warning Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, after multiple reported security compromises. Operators were instructed to take their servers offline immediately while developers prepared critical patches to address t...
content:
LNbits, the open-source Lightning Network wallet and payments platform, issued an emergency shutdown warning Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, after multiple reported security compromises. Operators were instructed to take their servers offline immediately while developers prepared critical patches to address the unfolding attacks.

Key Takeaways

  • LNbits urged all server operators to shut down immediately following a wave of reported attacks on Nov. 8.
  • A Bittipbot operator reported losing 2,285,545 satoshis after attackers created unauthorized accounts.
  • Developers expect security patches within 24 to 48 hours, while LNbits’ hosted service remains suspended.

LNbits Sounds the Alarm as Lightning Network Attacks Unfold

The security warning arrived at approximately 13:56 UTC on Nov. 8, when LNbits published an unusually urgent announcement through its official X account. Rather than advising operators to install an update at their convenience, developers called for an immediate shutdown of all running instances.

The LNbits X account said:

“All LNbits users should stop their LNbits servers IMMEDIATELY. Please forward this announcement. Following a wave of attacks, we have a number of security patches to push. Until then, it’s better to err on the side of caution. Updates to follow soon.”

Core contributor Ben Arc reinforced the directive, explaining that developers expected patches to become available within 24 to 48 hours. He also encouraged community members to circulate the warning to anyone operating LNbits infrastructure.

The trouble had surfaced earlier. At approximately 12:33 UTC, LNbits advised operators using its Paywall extension to disable the feature immediately while developers investigated a potential vulnerability. The subsequent systemwide shutdown warning suggested the security concerns extended beyond a single extension.

LNbits also suspended instances running through its hosted service, my.lnbits.com, with developers indicating that operations could resume within 24 hours once the necessary fixes were implemented.

Attackers Drain Lightning Funds as Operator Promises Reimbursement

One documented incident involved Dutch operator Kevin Ravensberg, whose LNbits instance supports Bittipbot, a Telegram-based tipping service.

According to Ravensberg, attackers created new accounts and withdrew 2,285,545 satoshis between 9:22 a.m. and 2 p.m. UTC on Nov. 8. The stolen amount equals approximately 0.02285545 BTC. Ravensberg pledged to reimburse affected Bittipbot users personally, although access to funds would remain restricted until developers addressed the vulnerabilities.

The reported sequence raises uncomfortable questions about LNbits’ account-management and authorization mechanisms. However, investigators have not publicly established the precise exploit responsible for the unauthorized withdrawals.

LNbits operates as a modular payment system connected to Lightning funding sources, including LND and Core Lightning. Its architecture supports separate wallets, application programming interfaces, payment terminals, tipping services and numerous optional extensions.

That flexibility also introduces additional software components requiring security oversight, particularly when installations are accessible over the public internet.

Lightning Network Security Troubles Extend Beyond LNbits

The emergency follows a difficult year for Lightning Network infrastructure, with developers confronting vulnerabilities across several prominent implementations, including Core Lightning, Lightning Development Kit (LDK), and Eclair.

In August, Core Lightning maintainers confronted numerous AI-assisted vulnerability reports, several of which exposed genuine security problems. Developers recommended emergency precautions while preparing fixes, and approximately 22% of Core Lightning nodes reportedly went offline during the disruption.

September and October brought additional security releases addressing denial-of-service attacks, channel-closing weaknesses, transaction-signing problems and potential fund losses.

LDK developers patched a particularly concerning reconnect vulnerability that could induce affected nodes to sign conflicting commitment transactions. Core Lightning, meanwhile, issued successive updates addressing memory exhaustion, channel-management weaknesses, and other security defects.

LNbits had already undergone security scrutiny earlier in 2026. An external review by V12 identified an authentication-cache bypass and a Paypal integration weakness, both reportedly corrected in version 1.6.0. There is currently no established connection between those previously patched defects and Sunday’s attacks.

Can Lightning Operators Safely Resume Service?

For now, LNbits operators face a straightforward instruction: Keep affected infrastructure offline until developers release and verify the necessary security patches. The project’s immediate priority is to contain further unauthorized withdrawals, identify the compromised components, and restore services without exposing additional funds.

The broader concern extends beyond one wallet platform. Lightning applications frequently combine payment infrastructure, authentication systems, and third-party extensions, meaning weaknesses outside the underlying payment protocol can still expose users to financial losses.

Sunday’s emergency illustrates a persistent distinction in cryptocurrency security: A functioning payment network does not guarantee the safety of every application built upon it. For LNbits, restoring service may prove easier than establishing precisely how attackers breached its defenses.

Moreover, according to newhedge.io stats, since late July, the Lightning Network has shed more than 1,100 BTC in capacity, retreating to levels last recorded in mid-2022.

title: FinCEN Moves to Cut MEXC Global Off From US Banks Over Alleged $16B Illicit Flows
summary: The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network says MEXC Global facilitated at least $16 billion in transactions linked to illicit activity and has…
content:
TL;DR: The US Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network says MEXC Global facilitated at least $16 billion in transactions linked to illicit activity and has issued a special measure prohibiting US financial institutions from processing transfers involving the exchange. The finding is a regulator’s allegation, not a judgment against every MEXC user.

The sharpest crypto enforcement story of the weekend came not from a trading chart but from the US Treasury. On November 6, FinCEN announced an order designed to cut exchange MEXC Global off from the US financial system. The agency said its investigation identified at least $16 billion of illicit transactions linked to sanctions evasion and cybercrime, including activity involving Iranian, North Korean and Russian actors.

The agency’s official announcement is unusually consequential because it is aimed at the banking connections surrounding a crypto trading venue. That differs from imposing a fine and asking a business to improve compliance while continuing to operate normally.

What the special measure actually does

FinCEN says the order prevents US financial institutions from processing funds transfers involving MEXC Global. In practical terms, the measure targets access to dollar banking rails and the financial intermediaries that might otherwise settle transfers for exchange-related activity. It does not mean that every blockchain transaction involving an address associated with the venue has technically stopped. Public blockchains and regulated bank transfers are different systems.

Nor is $16 billion presented as a figure for customer losses or the value of assets currently missing. It is FinCEN’s description of transactions it associates with illicit activity. Collapsing those categories into a sensational theft headline would distort the regulatory finding. The allegations should also be attributed to the Treasury rather than treated as a court determination that every named counterparty committed an offence.

The action sits within Operation Economic Outcast, a Treasury effort focused on sanctions evasion networks. For compliance teams, its significance is immediate: a payment that indirectly touches a prohibited counterparty can create exposure even where the final customer has no intention of engaging with a sanctioned entity.

Why an exchange’s bank access matters

Crypto exchanges rely on an ecosystem of counterparties, not just matching engines and onchain wallets. Payments companies, correspondent banks, custodians and stablecoin issuers may all be involved in moving customer money. When US institutions are barred from processing transfers involving a named exchange, those providers must reassess their screening and contractual arrangements.

We have already seen why financial plumbing matters during periods of market stress. In our coverage of the restrictions around European stablecoin trading, a regulatory perimeter changed the practical routes through which customers could access particular assets. FinCEN’s mechanism is different, but the distinction between holding a token and accessing a particular service remains useful.

There may be knock-on effects for liquidity and settlement, but these require evidence rather than guesswork. The order alone does not establish the amount of MEXC volume that depends on US banks or how quickly alternative compliant arrangements could be developed.

What users and counterparties should check

Customers should look for direct notices from the exchange and their own banks, and avoid relying on unsolicited messages promising to ‘unlock’ accounts. Impersonation and recovery scams often exploit confusion around enforcement action. Institutional firms should consult the actual order and their legal advisers rather than assume a generic announcement captures every relevant obligation.

The questions now are how the prohibition is implemented, what its effective conditions mean for counterparties, and whether the exchange provides a substantive response. For now, the verified news is a significant US banking restriction grounded in FinCEN’s stated findings—not proof that customers’ crypto balances have vanished.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Keplr Wallet Breach Triggers $6 Million in Transfers Across Cosmos
summary: A security vulnerability at Web3Auth has forced Cosmos wallet provider Keplr to suspend Google and Apple logins after private keys were exposed, triggering widespread unauthorized transactions. Blockchain investigators traced more than $6 million in transfers, although recovery operations complicate...
content:
A security vulnerability at Web3Auth has forced Cosmos wallet provider Keplr to suspend Google and Apple logins after private keys were exposed, triggering widespread unauthorized transactions. Blockchain investigators traced more than $6 million in transfers, although recovery operations complicate the actual theft total.

Key Takeaways

  • Keplr suspended Google and Apple logins on Nov. 7 following a security incident involving third-party authentication provider Web3Auth.
  • Bitquery identified approximately $6.01 million in wallet transfers across multiple Cosmos networks, but some transactions involved protective recovery efforts.
  • Recovery-phrase and hardware-wallet accounts remain unaffected, while Web3Auth and Keplr work to secure vulnerable social-login wallets.

Web3Auth Vulnerability Leaves Keplr Social Login Accounts Exposed

The trouble began Friday, Nov. 6, when Web3Auth disclosed a security issue affecting infrastructure used by third-party services. By early Saturday, Keplr was reporting unauthorized transactions involving accounts created through Google and Apple authentication, prompting the wallet provider to disable both login methods.

Josh Lee, co-founder of Chainapsis, the company behind Keplr, subsequently clarified that the vulnerability originated with Web3Auth rather than Keplr’s own software. Early estimates suggested approximately 20% of social-login accounts were affected, although only a fraction had reportedly been exploited.

The distinction matters because Keplr’s social-login feature relies on third-party key infrastructure rather than conventional user-controlled recovery phrases. That convenience simplifies cryptocurrency onboarding but creates dependencies absent from traditional hardware-wallet and seed-phrase arrangements.

Blockchain analytics company Bitquery examined transactions spanning Nov. 6-7, identifying extensive wallet-draining activity across Cosmos Hub, Osmosis, Celestia, Akash, Noble, Dydx, Babylon, and Injective.

Its investigation estimated that collector addresses received assets worth at least $6.01 million, based on valuations recorded Nov. 7. Cosmos Hub represented approximately $3.50 million, followed by Osmosis at $1.04 million and Injective at $615,000.

Why the $6 Million Keplr Theft Estimate Is Complicated

Bitquery’s analysis counted approximately 44,700 distinct private keys involved in the activity, with 86% of affected wallets on seven linked networks experiencing transfers after Keplr’s initial warning. Median wallet losses were just $1.34, although the largest individual transfer approached $325,000.

Investigators also documented approximately 1.96 million staked ATOM moving without the customary 21-day unbonding period. The transactions employed liquid staking mechanisms, converting positions into transferable share tokens while redirecting roughly $251,000 in staking rewards.

Yet subsequent disclosures introduced an important complication. Keplr and Web3Auth confirmed that white-hat recovery operations were using the exposed access path to move vulnerable assets into protective custody.

On Sunday, Nov. 8, Keplr identified recovery addresses that overlapped with several collector wallets examined by Bitquery. Consequently, the $6.01 million represents observed transfers, not a verified accounting of irrecoverable theft.

Keplr and Web3Auth Begin Recovery Efforts

Web3Auth maintains that funds transferred through its protective operations remain secure. Keplr, meanwhile, cautioned that some affected users might encounter unexpectedly empty balances because their assets had been relocated for safekeeping.

The companies have not disclosed the vulnerability’s precise technical cause, established a definitive loss figure or announced a comprehensive reimbursement schedule.

Users who created accounts through the global technology companies Google or Apple should avoid depositing additional assets, transfer remaining liquid holdings into newly secured wallets and disregard unsolicited recovery offers. Staked assets may require additional processing.

For now, the incident exposes an uncomfortable contradiction in cryptocurrency wallet design. Simplifying private-key management can make blockchain applications more accessible, but outsourcing authentication introduces another potential point of failure. Until protective transfers are reconciled with malicious withdrawals, the industry’s latest multimillion-dollar security scare remains as much an accounting mystery as a technical emergency.

title: OKX Freezes MEXC User Deposits Following Strict FinCEN Order
summary: Social media reports say some exchanges, including OKX, have begun flagging deposits from MEXC-linked addresses after the U.S. Treasury blacklisted the exchange for processing over $16 billion in illicit financial activity tied to sanctioned entities in Iran, Russia, and North Korea. MEXC Customers ...
content:
1. News
  2. Exchanges
  3. OKX Freezes MEXC User Deposits Following Strict FinCEN Order

Published:Nov 8, 2026, 12:13 PM EST

Social media reports say some exchanges, including OKX, have begun flagging deposits from MEXC-linked addresses after the U.S. Treasury blacklisted the exchange for processing over $16 billion in illicit financial activity tied to sanctioned entities in Iran, Russia, and North Korea.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 8, 2026, 12:13 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • FinCEN cut MEXC from the US financial system for allegedly processing $16B for sanctioned foreign actors.
  • In response, OKX immediately restricted direct transfers from MEXC and began freezing affected user funds.
  • MEXC claims operations remain smooth as it works with analytics firms to restore its safe address status.

MEXC Customers Face Transaction Holds After U.S. Treasury Blacklist Exchange

The U.S. Treasury Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) recently took action against MEXC, a top 20 cryptocurrency exchange, and it is starting to affect its customers.

MEXC users are complaining about deposit holds on exchanges like OKX when making direct transactions from their accounts after FinCEN issued an order cutting MEXC off from the U.S. financial system for serving as what the institution labeled a “hub for sanctioned actors,” processing over $16 billion for entities in Iran, Russia, and North Korea, even as the company recently cut support for users in Russia and Belarus.

Social media reports that called this situation into attention surged on social media, with users claiming that their deposits were frozen “under the vague excuse of coming from a ‘potentially high-risk address.'”

“We are not criminals. We are ordinary crypto users transferring our own assets between exchanges,” the user reiterated.

Star Xu, founder and CEO of OKX, clarified that while the FinCEN order only prohibited U.S. financial institutions from engaging in any transmittal of funds from or to MEXC Global, and that there was a 30-day transition period, the exchange had “already significantly strengthened its controls rather than waiting until the deadline.”

“OKX treats FinCEN special measures with a level of caution similar to sanctions. Under our compliance controls, funds associated with affected platforms may be frozen, and related accounts may be subject to further investigation,” Xu stressed, calling on users to avoid transferring funds directly from MEXC.

MEX CEO Vugar Usi stressed that operations at the exchange continue to run smoothly, even with increased withdrawal volumes. The company is working with analytics providers like Elliptic to remove the special risk classification from its addresses and return them to the original “exchange” category.

“I would like to stress that we take the concerns raised in FinCEN’s order seriously. We intend to engage constructively with FinCEN and have begun an independent review of our AML and sanctions controls,” he concluded.

Nonetheless, more users are worried about the status of their cryptocurrency wallets, wondering if just having interacted with MEXC addresses at some point would put their funds at risk without receiving a clear answer.

Before FinCEN’s designation, MEXC experienced a relevant rise in tokenized trading, with AI asset spot volume surging 88% and tokenized U.S. stock spot volume jumping 81% in September.

About the author

WRITTEN BYSergio Goschenko

Sergio is a cryptocurrency journalist based in Venezuela with 2,000+ articles published, cited in dozens of papers and reports.

title: Weekly Report: Crypto Market Erases $100B Rally as Bitcoin, XRP Prices Slide
summary: The crypto market endured a volatile first week of November, briefly gaining approximately $100 billion following the U.S. midterm elections before surrendering those gains amid a global technology stock sell-off. Post-Election Rally Gives Way to Global Market Sell-Off The crypto economy endured a v...
content:
The crypto market endured a volatile first week of November, briefly gaining approximately $100 billion following the U.S. midterm elections before surrendering those gains amid a global technology stock sell-off.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin fell 2.5% as crypto markets erased $100 billion in post-election gains amid a global sell-off.
  • XRP dropped over 7%, while NEAR plunged 15%, highlighting widespread weakness across major altcoins.
  • Zcash (ZEC) and tron (TRX) gained 3%, while gold-backed tokens rose over 4%, signaling potential defensive demand.

Post-Election Rally Gives Way to Global Market Sell-Off

The crypto economy endured a volatile first week of November, with its market capitalization rising by $100 billion following the U.S. midterm elections before surrendering those gains amid a broader sell-off across global financial markets.

Market data show the crypto economy began the week with a market capitalization barely above $2.7 trillion before bearish sentiment ahead of Election Day pushed it down to $2.67 trillion. However, as initial U.S. election results pointed to a shift in power in Washington, the crypto market staged a surprise rally, led by bitcoin, which surged from just above $75,000 to $81,000. By Nov. 5, the crypto economy’s total market capitalization had approached the $2.79 trillion mark.

However, as reports surfaced of proposed Democratic restrictions on crypto and data centers, technology stocks, especially those tied to artificial intelligence (AI), plunged, erasing trillions in market value. By Friday, Nov. 6, the total crypto market capitalization had dropped back below $2.64 trillion, highlighting the week’s severe volatility.

Bitcoin, which briefly dipped below $75,000 for the first time since late August, played a central role in the crypto market’s sharp swings. Despite the price fluctuations, the top cryptocurrency ended the week down 2.5%, falling from $77,845 to $75,877. A similar pattern emerged across several other digital assets, which posted impressive gains during the post-election rally only to surrender them following the technology stock sell-off.

Zcash, Tron and Gold-Backed Tokens Defy Market Downturn

Some digital assets, including XRP, suffered even steeper losses than bitcoin. Market data show that after briefly surpassing $1.32, XRP reversed course and continued sliding into Saturday, when it touched a multi-week low of $1.15. The downturn left XRP down more than 7% over the seven-day period.

Hyperliquid (HYPE) also recorded steep losses, falling more than 12%, while XLM and BCH declined approximately 10% and 12%, respectively. NEAR suffered an even sharper drop of 15%, while WLFI shed 7% during the period.

Nevertheless, a handful of digital assets outperformed the broader crypto market, including tron (TRX) and the privacy coin zcash (ZEC). Market data show both cryptocurrencies gained approximately 3%, while gold-backed tokens XAUT and PAXG rose 4.6% and 4.1%, respectively.

title: Binance CFO Kaiser Ng Exits After 5 Years, Justin Yek Takes Over Finance Leadership
summary:
Key Takeaways: After five years, CFO of Binance, Kaiser Ng stepped down to head other businesses. He will be replaced by Airwallex vice president of finance, Justin Yek. Ng will
The post Binance CFO Kaiser Ng Exits After 5 Years, Justin Yek Takes Over Finance Leadership appeared first on CryptoNinja...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • After five years, CFO of Binance, Kaiser Ng stepped down to head other businesses.
  • He will be replaced by Airwallex vice president of finance, Justin Yek.
  • Ng will pursue the opportunities in AI, Web3 tokenization, sports, entertainment and robotics.

Following the decision of its chief financial officer, Kaiser Ng, to resign, Binance is looking to replace him. Ng shared his recollections of the exchange business and announced his intentions to establish businesses based on new technologies and blockchain own assets.

  • Kaiser Ng Reflects on Five Years at Binance
  • Justin Yek Named as His Successor
    • Ng Plans New Ventures in AI and Web3

Kaiser Ng Reflects on Five Years at Binance

Ng announced his departure in a post on X, saying he had decided to pursue several projects of his own. He described his time at Binance as one of the most rewarding periods of his career, despite the challenges facing the crypto industry.

After five years as CFO of Binance, I have decided to go build something of my own.

The past ten years in the digital asset exchange space have felt surprisingly short, because I enjoyed what I was doing. Having passion for what you do is so important, and I will come back to this point. 8am to 2am became a work habit. When I felt exhausted past midnight, I would just look up at the Kobe Bryant’s statue standing in the corner of my office, and go right back to the grind!

It has been the privilege of my career to help steward the finances of the world’s largest digital asset exchange through a period that tested our industry in every way: bull and bear cycles, Operation Choke Point 2.0, and a regulatory landscape that evolved as quickly as the technology itself. Finance is seldom the loudest function in a company, but it is where trust is earned. Over these five years, we transformed Finance from a pure back-office function into one that consistently generates new ideas and revenue opportunities for the company. We became amazing problem solvers. Finance understood the products and metrics as well as the business units themselves. Proud of what we have built together, and I am pleased to hand the keys to Justin, our next CFO.

I want to take this opportunity to thank CZ, Yi, Richard, and the leadership team for their confidence and, above all, the amazing Binancians around the world whom I had the honor of working with. You are the reason the company stands where it does today. Binance is in very capable hands.

The company continues to grow and evolve with the successful launch of TradFi assets and AI-powered user interfaces. I’d like to express my gratitude to MGX for the trust; to our home regulator Abu Dhabi Global Market and all regulators we work closely with; and to our business partners, including BlackRock, Circle, Franklin Templeton, Mastercard, our banking partners and payment channels, as well as our advisors and auditors. Special thanks to Grant Thornton Singapore and everyone who has supported Binance.

As for what comes next, well, there isn’t just one project but several that I am passionate about particularly in sports and entertainment, from basketball and music, to GPUs, robotics, gold and collectibles. Bringing these real-world assets onto the blockchain through tokenization is a massive opportunity for the industry, and a big unlock for everyone. I welcome anyone with a passion in these areas to message me and potentially join my team. Even better if you love Kobe ;)

Moving from the CFO’s chair to the founder’s is a leap, and I take it with humility. I deeply believe it is where I can make a greater contribution to AI and Web3.

For now, thank you, Binance, for five remarkable years.

— Kaiser Ng (@kaizng) November 8, 2026

During his tenure, the exchange navigated bull and bear markets, regulatory changes and what Ng described as “Operation Choke Point 2.0.” He also said that he had to work long hours, at times from 8 a.m. until 2 a.m.

He noted one achievement, for instance, as Binance’s finance team evolved from a conventional back-office role to one that proactively provided business ideas and revenue opportunities.

Understand Binance products, business metrics and commercial operations to collaborate more closely with other departments, says Ng.

Read More: CZ Sends $965K to Giggle Academy, Retires Wallet After Meme Coin Chaos

Justin Yek Named as His Successor

Ng said he was giving Justin Yek the job of CFO. Reuters cited Yek as someone with long experience in the finance sector, most recently as vice president of finance for Airwallex. He stated that Binance had been preparing for the change of chairs for a full six months before the recent crypto breach.

It was revealed less than a week after Binance on Oct. 29 admitted to losing $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency. Ng’s resignation came after a “planned” transition, however, according to the exchange, so there is no linked relationship.

Ng Plans New Ventures in AI and Web3

Next, Ng’s next chapter will be multiple projects, not a single business. He specifically mentioned basketball, music, GPUs, robotics, gold and collectibles as areas that interest him.

Through tokenization, he believes he can now weave the reality of these businesses into blockchain networks. For him, this could provide new perspectives for the capabilities of electronic assets and make conventional assets more accessible.

Finally, Ng spoke about how he could make a bigger impact on AI and Web3 as a founder. He opened his new ventures to others who have an interest, implying that his working processes for the next project may have begun already.

Ng expressed his gratitude to Binance’s leadership, staff, regulators and business partners such as BlackRock, Circle, Franklin Templeton and Mastercard in his farewell message. He also pointed to the exchange’s expansion into TradFi assets and AI-powered user interfaces as signs of its continued development.

title: Anthropic Secures $3.4B Gas Power Deal to Fuel AI Data Centers, IPO Valuation Drops to $1.2T
summary: Anthropic is committing billions to secure its own electricity supply, underscoring how power availability is becoming a defining challenge for artificial intelligence expansion.
content:
Skip to content

Anthropic is committing billions to secure its own electricity supply, underscoring how power availability is becoming a defining challenge for artificial intelligence expansion.

The reported $3.4 billion agreement for 1.7 gigawatts of gas-fired generators comes as investors reassess the AI company’s IPO valuation following a sharp technology-stock selloff.

Anthropic Takes Over $3.4 Billion Generator Commitments

Anthropic has reportedly agreed to a $3.4 billion deal with OnePWR Solutions to secure 1.7 gigawatts of gas-fired power generators for its expanding AI data center operations. According to the Financial Times, the agreement was reached in late September and involves taking over existing equipment commitments for Caterpillar generators that the Texas-based supplier had ordered approximately two years earlier.

Anthropic secured a $3.4 billion deal with OnePWR Solutions for 1.7 GW of gas-fired generators to power its AI data centers. Source: Bloomberg via X

The transaction also includes engineering and construction capabilities needed to install the equipment. However, Anthropic is not acquiring OnePWR Solutions, and the supplier’s employees are not transferring to the AI company. The arrangement allows Anthropic to secure generators expected to become available soon and over the following two years, addressing supply delays affecting large power-generation equipment.

The Financial Times described the transaction as the largest known single purchase of power-generation equipment by an AI laboratory. The scale highlights how electricity procurement is becoming an essential part of the competition between companies developing increasingly powerful AI models.

Reuters reported the agreement on November 8 but said it could not independently verify the Financial Times report. Anthropic and OnePWR did not respond to requests for comment.

Electricity Shortages Push Anthropic Toward Natural Gas

The generator agreement reflects a growing challenge facing AI companies: securing enough electricity to operate increasingly demanding computing infrastructure. Training and running advanced AI models require large clusters of specialized processors, which consume substantial amounts of power and generate significant cooling requirements.

Anthropic addressed these constraints in its amended Form S-1 registration statement filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 2. The company identified electricity availability as a significant obstacle to developing and expanding data centers, noting that existing grid infrastructure was not designed to accommodate the rapid growth in AI-related demand.

The filing also explained that building new power-generation capacity, transmission infrastructure, and grid connections can take several years. Consequently, some planned Anthropic facilities will rely on dedicated natural gas-fired generation rather than depending entirely on utility-connected electricity.

The company explicitly acknowledged the financial and operational risks associated with this approach. Its filing stated that on-site natural gas generation exposes the business to “fuel price volatility and supply disruptions” outside its control. Anthropic also warned about pipeline capacity limitations, competition for natural gas supplies, and potential increases in transportation costs.

These arrangements offer a way to secure electricity for facilities where grid connections may not meet the required development schedule. However, they also introduce additional exposure to energy markets, fuel availability, and regulatory requirements.

Anthropic’s Infrastructure Commitments Approach $900 Billion

The generator purchase forms part of a much larger infrastructure expansion. Anthropic disclosed approximately $895.4 billion in aggregate committed spending through its purchase agreements and lease arrangements, substantially related to computing resources and infrastructure.

Anthropic disclosed approximately $895.4 billion in combined purchase and lease commitments as of and after September 30. Source: @DeItaone via X

According to the amended SEC filing, approximately $447.5 billion of these commitments are expected to be incurred before December 31, 2030. Most of the remaining obligations are scheduled between 2031 and 2045, while approximately $69.8 billion is due during the 12 months following September 30, 2026.

The company said it intends to fund these investments through operating revenue and capital raised from investors. Its infrastructure strategy includes securing data center capacity while gradually expanding the computing equipment deployed at those facilities.

Anthropic is not alone in facing these challenges. Other AI developers are also responding to growing electricity requirements and public concerns about data center expansion. OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar recently defended the company’s infrastructure plans and pledged to prevent its projects from increasing household electricity bills, as detailed in the report on OpenAI’s data center commitments.

The race for computing infrastructure is also extending beyond electricity procurement. As reported in Brave New Coin’s coverage of Moonshot AI’s Nvidia Blackwell GPU expansion, AI developers are pursuing additional access to advanced processors through international data center operators.

Together, these developments show how AI expansion increasingly depends on securing several interconnected resources, including processors, electricity, cooling infrastructure, and long-term financing.

Anthropic IPO Valuation Expectations Fall to $1.2 Trillion

Alongside its infrastructure expansion, Anthropic is preparing for a potential public-market debut. However, its expected IPO valuation has come under pressure following a substantial selloff across technology stocks.

Anthropic’s expected IPO valuation has fallen from nearly $2 trillion to $1.2–$1.3 trillion, amid a post-election AI and technology selloff that wiped trillions off market values. Source: @DeItaone via X

Walter Bloomberg reported on November 6 that prospective investors were discussing a valuation range of approximately $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion ahead of formal IPO marketing. Some potential buyers were considering a valuation as low as $1.1 trillion.

The revised expectations represent a significant change from earlier discussions that placed Anthropic’s potential valuation near $2 trillion. Investors had more recently considered a range of approximately $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion before the latest market decline altered their assessments.

The Nasdaq 100 fell approximately 6.4% on November 5, wiping out around $2.3 trillion in market value in a single session. The decline intensified concerns about elevated AI-related valuations, rising infrastructure costs, and the financial requirements associated with continued data center construction.

The technology selloff followed the November 3 U.S. midterm elections, adding another layer of uncertainty for companies planning large infrastructure investments. Political pressure surrounding data center development and electricity consumption has also become an important consideration for the technology industry.

For Anthropic, the valuation reset highlights the difference between strong business expansion and the price investors are prepared to pay for future growth. Although its computing capacity and revenue requirements continue to increase, the broader market environment is becoming less supportive of the exceptionally high valuations previously discussed.

Kalshi Traders Maintain Optimism About a Near-Term IPO

Despite the declining valuation expectations, prediction-market participants continue to assign relatively high probabilities to an upcoming Anthropic IPO milestone.

Kalshi’s market tracking the timing of an official IPO confirmation showed an 82% probability of the event occurring before December 1, 2026, as of November 8. The probability increased to 85% before January 1, 2027, and 91% before February 1, 2027.

Kalshi’s odds of an Anthropic IPO this month have risen to 85%, as the company reportedly targets an $80–$100 billion raise at a $1.25–$1.75 trillion valuation. Source: @wallstengine via X

These figures reflect market participants’ expectations rather than a confirmed listing schedule. Kalshi’s settlement rules also define an IPO confirmation through specific regulatory or listing milestones, including the SEC declaring the S-1 effective, the IPO being priced, or a securities exchange assigning a ticker.

Anthropic announced on October 26 that it had filed its Form S-1 registration statement with the SEC for a proposed public offering of Class A common stock. The company intends to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT.

However, the initial filing did not establish the number of shares to be offered or the proposed price range. The registration statement must also become effective before the securities can be sold.

Consequently, the high prediction-market probabilities indicate expectations for progress toward the public offering, not confirmation that trading will begin by any particular date.

Revenue Growth Faces a Test From Rising Infrastructure Costs

Anthropic’s financial performance provides additional context for its ambitious spending plans. Its amended SEC filing reported revenue of $33.2 billion for the first nine months of 2026, compared with approximately $2.5 billion during the same period in 2025.

Third-quarter revenue reached approximately $17 billion, reflecting rapidly expanding demand for the company’s Claude models and related products. Anthropic attributed the growth to successive model releases, increased usage, and broader adoption among enterprise customers.

However, operating expenses have also increased significantly. Compute and infrastructure costs reached approximately $18.8 billion during the first nine months of 2026, compared with $4.4 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier.

The company recorded an operating loss of approximately $1.26 billion for the nine-month period, even as adjusted operating income reached $4.1 billion. Its filing also highlighted that additional short-term computing capacity can carry substantially higher costs than longer-term arrangements.

Anthropic’s natural gas generator agreement therefore represents more than an equipment purchase. It is part of a broader effort to secure the physical resources required to support future computing demand while managing the cost and availability of electricity.

The developments also place two different aspects of the company’s growth under scrutiny. Its infrastructure commitments demonstrate the scale of its expansion ambitions, while the lower valuation discussions reflect investors’ changing assessment of the costs, risks, and financial requirements behind the AI industry.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto: Binance France is closing up shop in the country, as all accounts will be closed on Dec. 31. The US Treasury imposed financial sanctions on eight Canadian money-service companies it claims have done business with sanctioned ‌Iranian entities, and the Treasury also moved to cut MEXC off from the US financial system over alleged illicit transactions.

Binance France emails announce closure of accounts Dec. 31

Binance France is closing up shop in the country. Customers have been notified by email during early November, according to media reports.

All accounts will be closed on Dec. 31, and any assets left on the exchange will be charged monthly fees starting on Nov. 29, Cryptoast, Crypto Briefing and other media reported on Saturday, citing emails sent to users by Binance.

On that date, accounts still maintaining a balance will pay a monthly maintenance fee of 0.025% of the balance, or a minimum of 10 USDC, a stablecoin tracking the US dollar.

To avoid fees, withdrawals must be completed by Nov. 29, the exchange said.

US sanctions Canadian money-exchange firms over Iran ties

The US Treasury imposed financial sanctions on eight Canadian money-service companies it claims have done business with sanctioned ‌Iranian entities.

These companies facilitated the exchange of Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets, enabling international transactions, a US Treasury Department statement said on Friday.

The sanctions, which serve to isolate the companies from the dollar-based financial system, are the latest in a series of Treasury moves against firms outside the US.

These businesses have facilitated transactions with sanctioned Iranian digital asset exchanges, as well as with digital asset addresses associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), according to the Treasury.

US Treasury cuts off MEXC over alleged $16B in illicit transactions

The US Department of Treasury on Friday issued an order to cut cryptocurrency exchange MEXC Global off from the US’ financial system after accusing it of facilitating at least $16 billion in transactions linked to sanctions evasion, cybercrime and other illicit activity.

The Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) asserted that MEXC handled transactions involving sanctioned groups in Iran, Russia and North Korea between May 2021 and May 2026. This included around $1.5 billion in transactions linked to Russian sanctions evasion, according to the official press release.

The order effectively bans US financial institutions from processing money transfers involving MEXC and will take effect 30 days after it is published in the Federal Register. 

“Financial institutions cannot have it both ways: Either you support the Iranian regime, or you have access to the U.S. financial system,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Treasury will continue to sever the Iranian regime’s economic lifelines and thwart its desperate attempts to circumvent U.S. sanctions using digital assets.”

The action is part of Operation Economic Outcast, a US Treasury campaign launched in August with aims to cut off financial entities that help Iran evade sanctions.

According to DefiLlama, the exchange held about $4.48 billion in total assets as of Friday. Cointelegraph contacted MEXC for comment but had not received a response by publication.

title: Binance France emails announce closure of its users’ accounts on Dec. 31
summary: Any assets left on the exchange will be charged monthly fees starting on Nov. 29, company says.
content:
Binance France is closing up shop in the country. Customers have been notified by email during early November, according to media reports.

All accounts will be closed on Dec. 31, and any assets left on the exchange will be charged monthly fees starting on Nov. 29, Cryptoast, Crypto Briefing and other media reported on Saturday, citing emails sent to users by Binance.

On that date, accounts still maintaining a balance will pay a monthly maintenance fee of 0.025% of the balance, or a minimum of 10 USDC, a stablecoin tracking the US dollar.

To avoid fees, withdrawals must be completed by Nov. 29, the exchange said.

A Binance email cited by Cryptoast said: “Due to the orderly cessation of activities, your Binance France account will close as of December 31, 2026. If you have not withdrawn your crypto-assets as of December 31, 2026, this message constitutes a notification of our intention to consider your account inactive, in accordance with our Terms of Use. This can result in the conversion, transfer or other processing of your crypto-assets.”

Key services restricted in June

Related: Binance’s EU services face scrutiny over licensing exemption: Report

Cointelegraph reported in late June that Binance had notified European Union users access to key services would be restricted after the exchange failed to secure Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulatory authorization from a member state before a July 1 deadline.

On Sunday, a Binance spokesperson responded to a Cointelegraph query, saying, “Following the end of the MiCA transition period, Binance is progressively restricting certain services for affected users, in line with the schedule previously communicated to them.”

Though asked specifically about reports similar emails had also been sent to users in Spain and Belgium, the spokesperson made no mention of them.

According to media reports, Binance’s global client base counts at least 300 million customers, while the app was downloaded more than 4 million times in the EU last year.

title: Tornado Cash-Linked Wallet Sells ETH to Buy Zcash on Hyperliquid
summary:
Key Takeaways: In a 20-hour period, a wallet transferred 1,670 ETH valued at around $3.73 million from Tornado Cash to Hyperliquid. The ETH was exchanged for 2,959 ZEC, worth approximately
The post Tornado Cash-Linked Wallet Sells ETH to Buy Zcash on Hyperliquid appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • In a 20-hour period, a wallet transferred 1,670 ETH valued at around $3.73 million from Tornado Cash to Hyperliquid.
  • The ETH was exchanged for 2,959 ZEC, worth approximately $3.73 million at the time of the acquisition.
  • Lookonchain noted the transaction, while Arkham noted the ETH-to-ZEC activity.

According to Lookonchain, an onchain wallet turned around about $3.73 million of Ethereum from Tornado Cash to Hyperliquid and then cashed it out for Zcash. This activity compares 1,670 ETH and 2,959 ZEC have been bought in 20 hours.

This is an interesting transaction as the wallet is more than just a tool to transfer funds between platforms. Rather, it sold a good amount of ETH and made use of the proceeds to construct its collections of ZEC.

  • 1,670 ETH Deposited and Sold on Hyperliquid
  • Arkham Tracks the ETH-to-ZEC Activity
    • ZEC Becomes the Destination for the $3.73M ETH Sale

1,670 ETH Deposited and Sold on Hyperliquid

Over the last 20 hours, 1,670 ETH valued at around $3.73 million has been staked on Hyperliquid using Tornado Cash, says Lookonchain in a post on X. The money was then used to buy ZEC. Lookonchain reported that it acquired the total sum of 2,959 ZEC which translates to the equivalent of around $3.73 million.

It appears the hacker is selling ETH to buy ZEC!

Over the past 20 hours, 1,670 $ETH ($3.73M) from #TornadoCash was deposited into Hyperliquid and sold to buy 2,959 $ZEC ($3.73M).

https://t.co/XDlBb5fGSv https://t.co/y2lW20A6bn

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 8, 2026

These are direct Ethereum-to-Zcash conversions. Instead of withdrawing ETH from the mixer and storing it in the wallet, the wallet has handled the funds on Hyperliquid to swap them for another cryptocurrency.

The corresponding number of 1670 ETH was transferred from Tornado Cash, and 2959 ZEC was then purchased via the respective trades that are reported.

Read More: ICE Partners With Trade[XYZ] to Bring $650B Hyperliquid Futures Market to the U.S.

Arkham Tracks the ETH-to-ZEC Activity

Lookonchain also shared an Arkham entity link associated with the activity, labeled ETH-to-ZEC. The tracking page provides an additional reference for examining the wallet’s onchain movements.

Another Arkham entity link pertaining to the activity is ETH-to-ZEC which it was also looking at. The tracking pages are additional references to analyse the onchain tracking of the wallet.

The price of around $3.73 million on both sides of the trade is stated by Lookonchain. As stated, these are reported transaction values and not intended to be an indication that the wallet still contains the same amount of ZEC.

The use of Tornado Cash is also pertinent information to be traced but is not enough to conclude the staking of the assets or even determine who is the owner of the wallet.

ZEC Becomes the Destination for the $3.73M ETH Sale

The big change is that the wallet gave away 1670 ETH and exchanged for 2959 ZEC in the 20-intraday trading period. This isn’t just a simple transfer between wallets, but a substantial conversion from ETH to ZEC.

It was a fraud where hackers sell some ETH coins to acquire some ZEC by virtue of their activities, Lookonchain said. The transaction information, however, only confirms the movement and reported swap, not who owns the wallet or what the origin of the funds are apart from the connection to Tornado Cash.

title: Ethereum (ETH) Price Prediction: Whale Accumulation Builds as $2,350 Reclaim Could Restart the Recovery
summary: Ethereum (ETH) is trading at a critical juncture as bulls defend key support levels while bearish pressure persists, leaving traders watching for the next major price move.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ETH

Ethereum (ETH) is trading at a critical juncture as bulls defend key support levels while bearish pressure persists, leaving traders watching for the next major price move.

Ethereum is starting November at an important point in its recovery. According to Brave New Coin, ETH is trading near $2,230, with price now sitting close to the same support region where whale buying, long-term accumulation signals and several technical recovery setups are beginning to overlap.

Ethereum Tests $2,219 Support as $2,350 Caps the Recovery

Ethereum is trading around one of the more important technical areas on the daily chart. Daan Crypto Trades highlights the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement near $2,219, with price currently attempting to stabilize around that level after the latest decline.

The first resistance sits at the daily 200EMA around $2,315, but the more important hurdle remains the horizontal area near $2,350. ETH has already reacted from lower levels, yet previous recovery attempts have struggled around this zone. A sustained move above $2,350 would therefore better signal that buyers are regaining control.

Support remains layered underneath the market. The 0.65 Fibonacci retracement sits near $2,188, while the daily 200MA is positioned around $2,158. Losing both would weaken the current recovery structure and leave Ethereum vulnerable to another leg lower.

Ethereum is holding near the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement around $2,219, while $2,315 and $2,350 remain the main levels bulls need to recover. Source: Daan Crypto Trades via X.

ETH Consolidation Could Set Up the Next Expansion

The current weakness does not necessarily rule out a larger recovery. Crypto analyst Joep Gerla points to a pattern Ethereum has already followed twice, where several weeks of sideways movement were followed by much sharper expansion moves.

The latest structure is beginning to resemble another compression phase, with ETH trading around $2,319 after falling roughly 21% from the recent range high. The rising trendline underneath price is now becoming increasingly important, while the nearby $2,220-$2,190 region remains the lower support area that needs to hold if the structure is going to remain bullish.

The previous two consolidations were followed by rallies of roughly 36% and 19.5%, and Gerla’s current projection maps another potential expansion of around 37%. If ETH price can hold the trendline and recover through the $2,460-$2,500 area, the next larger upside zone comes into view around $2,680-$2,780, with the projected Ethereum price prediction extending toward roughly $3,000.

A clean break above the current range would strengthen the case for another expansion phase, while a sustained loss of the rising trendline and $2,190-$2,220 support would weaken the comparison with the previous setups.

Ethereum markup phase could target $2,680-$3,000. Source: Joep Gerla via X.

Whale Accumulation Builds Despite ETF Selling

Ethereum’s larger-holder activity is beginning to show a clear split. In a post on X Lookonchain reports that whale address 0x4AB7 purchased another 3,300 ETH worth approximately $7.41 million, taking its total accumulation over the past week to roughly 13,077 ETH valued near $29.95 million.

Source: Lookonchain via X

That buying has taken place while ETH remains close to the lower end of its recent range, suggesting some larger holders are using the weakness to build exposure rather than waiting for a confirmed breakout. The $2,200 area therefore becomes more important if this accumulation continues.

At the same time, ETF-related selling remains a drag. Whale Insider reports that BlackRock clients sold approximately $90.76 million worth of ETH, showing that institutional flows are still moving in the opposite direction from the whale accumulation seen on-chain.

For now, Ethereum is sitting between those two forces. Continued whale buying would support the recovery case, but a slowdown in ETF selling would make that demand much more meaningful. If both begin moving in the same direction, the current base would have a stronger foundation for a broader recovery.

Longer-Term Ethereum Forecast Points Toward $3,500-$5,000

The higher-timeframe picture offers a more ambitious scenario if Ethereum can complete the current base. ZAYRO’s chart compares the previous distribution and markdown phase with what appears to be a developing accumulation structure around the recent lows.

The earlier cycle moved through several stages of distribution before price entered a prolonged markdown. The current setup is being interpreted as the opposite process, with Ethereum moving out of that decline and attempting to establish an accumulation range before a possible markup phase.

If price can successfully transition, then the ETH chart places $3,500 as the first larger recovery area, followed by $4,000 and eventually the previous highs around $5,000. Those targets remain well above the immediate market, which is why holding the current base and recovering the nearby resistance levels comes first.

Ethereum’s longer-term targets are in the range of $3,500, $4,000, and $5,000. Source: ZAYRO via X.

Ethereum Price Analysis: $2,350 Remains the Main Barrier

Ethereum is currently trading in a difficult part of the chart. Price is holding close to the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement near $2,219, while the daily 200EMA around $2,315 sits directly above the market and continues to limit the recovery.

Ethereum price is trading at around $2,230, up 0.61% in the last 24 hours. Source: Brave New Coin

The more important level remains $2,350. ETH has already shown that it can react from the lower support area, but a move back above this zone would provide much stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control. Until then, the latest rebound remains vulnerable to another rejection.

Below current price, $2,188 and the daily 200MA near $2,158 form the next support band. Holding those levels would keep the recovery structure alive, while a sustained break lower would suggest Ethereum still needs more time to form a durable base.

Final Thoughts: What Could Drive ETH’s Next Expansion?

Ethereum’s next larger move may depend on whether the current period of weakness develops into accumulation rather than another leg lower. Whale buying has continued despite the pullback, and several longer-term charts are beginning to point toward the possibility of a broader markup phase once the present consolidation is complete.

For the broader Ethereum Price Prediction, the first real improvement would come from ETH recovering $2,350 and beginning to hold above the daily trend levels again. If that happens, attention can shift toward $2,500-$2,700 before the larger $3,500 becomes relevant. If not, the market may remain range-bound for longer while buyers continue building around the lower support zone.

title: Silver Price Forecast Puts $52.75 in Focus Before the December Fed Meeting
summary: Silver is trying to break a difficult selling trend and return to a long-term buying trend, but the chart shows a significant ceiling that could hold the market down.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAG

Silver is trying to break a difficult selling trend and return to a long-term buying trend, but the chart shows a significant ceiling that could hold the market down.

The metal dropped from the $58 region in October to a low near $49, then bounced back toward the $51.30 area before easing to $50.78, according to market data on TradingView.

The two-hour candle saw the price ending at $50.7750, which was a 0.29% drop. Whether or not buyers can reclaim $51.74 and break $52.75, or if the rebound is lost under resistance, may be the key to the coming week.

Silver’s Rebound Remains Below a Key Resistance Band

The two-hour chart indicates the formation of a fall channel beginning from about October 21. But silver then lost horizontal support near $52.75 on October 29, pushing its slide down to $49.00 at the beginning of November.

That dip was defended by the buyers, and a modest recovery was pushed back to $51.30, but the pullback seems to have shown that the broader pullback was far from over.

This reserved outlook is supported by the Ichimoku indicator. It shows the reference readings around $50.61 and $51.74. Source: TradingView

A downward cloud forms overhead, and silver is slightly higher than the lower reading but is lower than the higher one. The $52.7489 line is then an upside test rather than an upside support, not shown as such. The buyers must recover the level of the indicator’s resistance and cross the horizontal barrier to confirm the reversal.

The latest low is the definite support on the image. Retaining it above the surface would give the opportunity for another rescue attempt. If, however, the rejection keeps the sellers on top below $51.74, then it would be repeated. If the price finds support at $48.00, the next psychological level could be reached if the price breaks below $49.00, which is not confirmed by the chart at this time.

Seasonal Chart Shows 2026 Lagging Earlier Years

Meanwhile, another TradingView chart shows a comparison of silver’s performance in 2024 vs. 2025 and 2026. It shows 2026 down 28.67% by early November, compared with a 21.28% gain in 2024 and a 142.33% advance in 2025 at the corresponding point.

This comparison is meant to highlight silver’s underperformance this year, following its stellar performance in 2025. Source: TradingView

That seasonal display isn’t a forecast. The advance for the year 2025 was much larger than usual, and there is no repeatable pattern for this. However, the 2026 line has been negative for most of the second half of the year, with little sign of a positive seasonal trend. Price confirmation is more important than taking for granted that November will be like previous years.

December Fed Meeting Puts Inflation and Jobs Data in Focus

Markets will closely watch monetary policy, as it is expected to be a primary factor ahead of the Federal Reserve’s meeting on December 8–9. In the lead-up, inflation reports, employment data, Treasury yields, and a changing value of the U.S. dollar can have a profound impact on expectations regarding the next policy change.

The recent employment report has added to the uncertainty. The dollar and Treasury yields strengthened as U.S. job growth was better than expected, Reuters reported on November 6. Traders pushed the chances of an increase in the interest rate in December up to 81%, up from 72.8% prior to the report.

Silver is generally not paid interest on it and is traded in dollars, so higher yields and a stronger dollar can be a negative for silver. If inflation were lower or job growth were weaker, then it would ease those pressures by dampening further demand for tightening.

Physical-market conditions also are important but may be less significant in the coming few sessions. Silver appears to be more responsive to interest-rate expectations and is less supported than gold, while there is less physical demand in the solar sector, according to Sucden Financial’s fourth-quarter outlook.

It also identifies constrained inventories as a potential buffer to more serious losses. The biggest influence for the upcoming week is more likely to be on the side of rate expectations. The coming week’s Silver Price Scenarios are presented below. Silver price scenarios for the upcoming week are presented below.

Bearish Scenario

The bearish case prevails as silver is trading below the overhead Ichimoku cloud as well as $51.74. If the price doesn’t come back to the area, it could push the price up to $50.00 and then to the recent $49.00 low. If the price breaks below $49.00, this should be a sign that the rebound is losing momentum and the $48.00 psychological level may be near. A continued recovery in U.S. data or upward yield pressure or renewed dollar strength would support this trend.

Bullish Scenario

The bulls must break above the resistance level of $52.75 and rally back to $51.74 to confirm the bulls are in charge. If the price closes above $52.75 for 2 hours or more, then it will be a better indication that the breakdown is out of control. It may be a step towards the 54.50-55.00 resistance level. That would require some less-than-tough US data, a reduction in yields, or a weaker dollar.

The week ahead’s overall outlook is neutral. The $49.00 level has found support, and the downward trend and bearish Ichimoku cloud are preserved. The 52.75 to 51.74 range will be the crucial area to see if buyers are able to take control.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Which of the following is the most critical level of resistance for silver?

The short-term indicator resistance is at $51.74. The key level to watch is the $52.75 mark, which silver must retake to improve its bullish outlook.

2. What is silver’s most important level of support?

The chart provided highlights the clearest support level in recent times to be around $49.00. An extended move below that level may bring the psychological $48.00 level into play.

3. What is needed to validate a bullish turn in silver?

A 2-hour close above $52.75 followed by further buying activity would increase the chances that the downtrend of recent activity is likely to be fading.

4. What would be the probable reaction of silver in the event of a negative outcome by the December FOMC meeting?

A more hawkish Fed sentiment could help to boost the dollar and Treasury yields, which would weigh on silver. Easier monetary policy expectations would be bolstered by softer inflation and employment data.

5. Does the seasonal chart suggest silver will rally in November?

No. The performance comparisons in the chart are historical, not indicative of any particular season. Silver is still in the red at 28.67% as of the provided snapshot in 2026.na
