title: Lithium Price Rebound Faces a Test as China Futures Volatility Returns
summary: After months of relentless selling, lithium is making a comeback, with its price in China's primary index rising to CNY 91,700 per tonne, though a steep monthly drop suggests the recovery is tenuous.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: Li

After months of relentless selling, lithium is making a comeback, with its price in China's primary index rising to CNY 91,700 per tonne, though a steep monthly drop suggests the recovery is tenuous.

Investors are now watching to see if the rebound has become a rally as futures volatility is rising and U.S. energy policy is entering a new chapter as battery demand renews, buoying investors.

The Market Is Struggling to Find Direction

The lithium carbonate market in China shows signs of a potential rebound, but the recovery is fragile. According to the provided Trading Economics chart, the price of lithium is projected to reach CNY 91,700 per tonne by November 5, 2026.

It has risen 14.05% year over year but dropped 26.61% month over month. This comparison reveals how fast gains in the past have been wiped out in recent sales.

The one-year chart shows the magnitude of the correction. The price of lithium rose from around CNY 80,000 per tonne to CNY 180,000 in early 2026. Source: TradingEconomics

The price later jumped to about CNY 200,000 in May and then started a long downward trend. There were several attempts to regain the previous momentum, but they were unsuccessful. Close to the low end of the annual trading range, the market had returned by November. The structure indicates that sellers still had the upper hand for the moment, even with the recent price stability.

Futures trading provides a more real-time view. The Futures Exchange of Guangzhou’s January 2027 contract closed at CNY 90,800 on Nov 5, posting a 2.76% rise. The December 2026 contract settled at CNY 92,160, up 1.72%. The January contract, on the other hand, had reached CNY 88,360 when it closed on Nov. 4 after dropping 1.80% during the session.

Strong selling pressure is thus expected to be present before the rebound is considered a confirmation of a bull market reversal. The latest contract references are given in the market data and lithium futures contract history published by SMM on November 5.

Supply, Battery Demand, and Inventories Could Shape the Next Move

The next big driver will be whether battery makers buy more to make up for the supply. The demand for lithium is subject to the production of electric vehicles, the installation of battery storage systems, and the programs of producers. If orders are stronger, producers would be encouraged to replenish inventories, which would bolster prices. Weaker order activity for batteries or slower sales, however, might lead to fewer buyers competing for the available suppliers.

It is particularly important to look at inventory trends. During the week ending Oct. 30, the battery-grade lithium carbonate prices averaged CNY 96,100 per tonne at the Shanghai Metals Market, according to the market. It also noted that the most-traded futures contract had dipped 8.4% to CNY 88,360.

Inventories in the industry fell during that week, but smelter inventories rose. That’s important because long-term pressure downstream doesn’t necessarily translate to pressure throughout the production chain. The investors should watch out for real inventory declines, processing volume, and new orders before assuming that the latest recovery is the right one. SMM industry update.

From a technical perspective, the next price level to monitor is CNY 90,000. A possible bounce back to CNY 95,000–100,000 would be aided by such an action as holding above it. If it keeps rising above CNY 100,000, it will be more convincing that buyers are coming back. On the other hand, if the selling persists below CNY 90,000, the CNY 85,000 range could get exposed, which is the previous low area in the chart. These are monitoring levels, not price guarantees.

US Midterm Election Aftermath Adds Policy Uncertainty

A Democrat won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 U.S. midterm elections. The price action in the financial markets started with a strong recovery in the key US shares following overnight volatility.

The dollar and yields on U.S. Treasuries also declined in early trading, and investors had to rethink the odds of legislative dysfunction. But these are mainly movements across the general financial markets and not a confirmed reaction in the lithium futures market. Market reaction.

The election has a profound impact on lithium investors because of its implications for future U.S. energy, trade, and industrial policies. Modifications of battery incentive & support, electric-vehicle support, tariffs, and critical mineral supply-chain programs may affect investment decisions.

Changes to the policy landscape could push back some projects, and ongoing support for domestic mineral production could attract investment away from China. However, Congress does not set the price for lithium in China. Meanwhile, production levels, inventories, battery orders, and export flows in China are more direct drivers.

For investors, the weeks ahead are a time of confirmation, not anticipation. The recovery would be bolstered by a sustained upward breakout from CNY 95,000, as well as continued inventory draws and improved battery orders. The risk that the inventory would continue to build up, due to failure to collect CNY 90,000, would be heightened, along with subdued demand from the downstream market. The election has a longer-term impact on investment in the United States, but China’s supply/demand imbalance will probably govern lithium’s next move.

title: $106M Crypto Theft Hits EU Entity, Solana MEV Bot King Drained for Another $786K
summary:
Key Takeaways: An anonymous EU firm could have lost over $106 million in various exchanges. The suspected attacker transferred USDC and USDT into ETH and XMR and cross-chain. Another Solana
The post $106M Crypto Theft Hits EU Entity, Solana MEV Bot King Drained for Another $786K appeared first on Cr...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • An anonymous EU firm could have lost over $106 million in various exchanges.
  • The suspected attacker transferred USDC and USDT into ETH and XMR and cross-chain.
  • Another Solana arbitrage bot known as King was singled out and slashed for approximately $786,000.

Crypto investigators continue to monitor two huge security breaches, totaling over $106 million in suspected stolen funds and another $786,000 worth of funds drained from an aging Solana trading bot.

The bigger case is still open but the victim and the exchanges and attacker still were not identified.

  • EU Entity May Have Lost Over $106M in Crypto
  • ZachXBT Rules Out Lazarus Group
    • Stolen Funds Move Beyond Freezable Stablecoins
    • Solana MEV Bot King Loses Another $786K

EU Entity May Have Lost Over $106M in Crypto

Blockchain investigator ZachXBT said an unnamed EU entity is suspected of losing more than $106 million from accounts held at several centralized crypto exchanges on Nov. 1.

Presumptive stolen funds were siphoned off at first in terms of USDC and USDT. ZachXBT released 11 addresses that were associated with the activity, but did not disclose any of the victims or how exchange accounts were opened.

The operant suspected attacker then rapidly reconfigured the asset trail during the next 24-hours.

In addition to USDC being swapped into ether, there were also funds transferred via instant exchange platforms like WellWallet and Kyrrex. Using Wagyu some assets were converted into privacy coin Monero, other assets moved over several blockchain networks.

Read More: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen

ZachXBT Rules Out Lazarus Group

The laundering activity does not seem to follow one of the patterns seen with the North Korea-related Lazarus Group, ZachXBT further said. Although who did the actual theft has not been determined, he said he had a “high degree of confidence” that it was not made by Lazarus.”

The particular is significant, as it comes after the big cyber breakout of cryptocurrencies occurred recently and brought North Korean cyber gangs back into the spotlight. There is, however, no evidence of the EU incident being related to those operations at the moment.

Stolen Funds Move Beyond Freezable Stablecoins

The transition towards stablecoins to ETH and XMR might hinder recoveries. The USDC/USDT issuers are able to freeze tokens on certain addresses; assets like Ether do not have a centralized issuer with similar capabilities. Monero poses yet another challenge as the Privacy features of the platform strip all the details away from transactions.

The speed of using instant exchanges and cross-chain bridges also makes the money trail more complex, allowing investigators to trace activity through various networks and services.

The EU firm in question and the exchanges in question have not confirmed this lack of funds.

Read More: Binance $5.5B Hack Exposed: 50 EIP-7702 Nonces Opened One Hot Wallet in Minutes

Solana MEV Bot King Loses Another $786K

Another incident struck older Solana arbiter King, one of the network’s automated trading bots. Onchain Lens stated that the bot lost approximately $786,000, comprising approximately 4,260 WSOL, 191 SOL and $366,000 worth of stablecoins. Prior to the incident, King had reported to have made about $7.2 million in lifetime profits.

SOLANA MEV BOT KING DRAINED OF $786K 💀

King, one of Solana’s oldest arbitrage bots with $7.2M in lifetime PnL, was drained of ~$786K, including 4.26K $WSOL, 191 $SOL and $366K in stablecoins.

Drainers:
BHRayETPjvgg3BCr9H82V1D6NRwxu5v44JAaVuaod3jU

Forwarder:
Ddmy5oM8xtTs1EBC6eF2SZwQfBreewQpFgtUDm51Hkqj

Victim: 7dGrdJRYtsNR8UYxZ3TnifXGjGc9eRYLq9sELwYpuuUu

— Onchain Lens (@OnchainLens) November 2, 2026

Onchain Lens was also able to locate the suspect drainer wallet, forward wallet, and the victim wallet’s address. It’s not yet been revealed what specific way was used to access the monitoring account and if the wallet was compromised through this or a different means.

title: TRON Tops Ethereum in USDT With $92.25B Stablecoin Supply and $2.18T Q3 Transfers
summary:
Key Takeaways: TRON has been ahead of Ethereum with an average trade size of USDT worth $90.75 billion within Q3. Supply of stablecoins hit an all-time high of $92.25 billion,
The post TRON Tops Ethereum in USDT With $92.25B Stablecoin Supply and $2.18T Q3 Transfers appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • TRON has been ahead of Ethereum with an average trade size of USDT worth $90.75 billion within Q3.
  • Supply of stablecoins hit an all-time high of $92.25 billion, and transfers valued at $2.18 trillion.
  • The number of transactions fell to 1.08 billion, but network revenues dropped to $693.21 million.

During the third quarter of 2026, TRON’s stablecoin settlement capability exceeded Ethereum in terms of the average stablecoin USDT supply and also recorded peaks on a number of network metrics.

According to Token Terminal’s latest quarterly report, balances of stablecoins, addresses held and monthly active users all reached new record highs.

https://t.co/qHyVVcR8Wb

— Token Terminal 📊 (@tokenterminal) November 2, 2026

  • TRON Takes the Lead in USDT Supply
  • Stablecoin Transfers Reach $2.18 Trillion
    • TRON Processes 1.08B Transactions
    • Revenue Falls Despite Record Network Activity

TRON Takes the Lead in USDT Supply

The average USDT in TRON is USD 90.75 billion during Q3 which is 4.11% higher from that of the previous quarter and 13.74% up from a year ago. Ethereum, on the other hand, had a $87.73 billion average, which is down 7.59% from a year ago. That resulted in a total of 49.49% of USDT being held in the 12 networks monitored by Token Terminal.

TRON first grabbed an advantage and held it for a bit until July 16, when it temporarily overtook Ethereum and remained in front for the rest of the quarter. A record $92.25 billion in stablecoins were established in total, increasing by about 4.18% compared to Q2 and 14.58% compared to last year. This amount climbed to $93.88 billion as of the end of September.

Read More: Justin Sun’s $2.25B Crypto Portfolio Includes $1.09B in SUSDS Across 10 Blockchains

Stablecoin Transfers Reach $2.18 Trillion

The activity on the stablecoins was also strong. In total, TRON powered $2.18 trillion worth of stablecoin transactions in the Q3, that’s 4.17% higher than in the prior quarter. The number of average stablecoin holder addresses has reached a new high of 76.53 million in 40.45% of the stablecoin’s total addresses on 45 chains tracked in the report.

A stablecoin transfer volume amounted to 23.67 times the average supply over the course of this quarter, with the average dollar value of a stablecoin on TRON transferring approximately every 3.89 days.

TRON Processes 1.08B Transactions

Network activity was close to record levels at 1.08 billion transactions, Q3. It represented an 31.19% increase from a year ago and the sixth consecutive quarterly uptick in the number of transactions. The average throughput was 135.76 transactions per second.

The company reported an average of 17.81 million users per month during the quarter, which is an increase of 8.71% from the second quarter and 21.86% compared to the same quarter in the previous year. Transaction growth also led to active-address growth, with each active address becoming part of 60.60 transactions during the quarter, up from 56.29 a year ago.

Revenue Falls Despite Record Network Activity

The network value of TRON has declined in the third quarter of 2018, decreasing 3.10% from the previous quarter and 34.40% year over year to $693.21 million. Particularly, transaction costs were lower, accounting for most of the drop. According to data, average fees dropped to $0.64 in August, down a staggering 50.20% from a year ago due to TRON dropping its Energy price in the same month.

Even taking into account lower fees, Token Terminal estimated that TRON was the biggest L1/L2 network by revenue among the networks in their comparison in the previous quarter with 93.18% of revenue.

title: Mercado Bitcoin Freezes Deposits and Withdrawals After $40M Crypto Security Alert
summary:
Key Takeaways: Mercado Bitcoin blocked deposits and withdrawals after it spotted a security incident. According to the company, Hypernative has spotted more than $40 million in suspiciously sized transfers on
The post Mercado Bitcoin Freezes Deposits and Withdrawals After $40M Crypto Security Alert ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Mercado Bitcoin blocked deposits and withdrawals after it spotted a security incident.
  • According to the company, Hypernative has spotted more than $40 million in suspiciously sized transfers on 10 blockchains.
  • The exchange says it has not compromised customer funds or data during the investigation.

Cryptocurrency exchange Mercado Bitcoin has temporarily suspended withdrawals and deposits after security problems. Investigations have raised questions over the volume of off-chain activity, but funds and data are not affected, the company said.

  • Mercado Bitcoin Suspends Deposits and Withdrawals
  • More Than $40 Million in Suspicious Transfers Reportedly Flagged
    • Exchange Publishes Wallet Addresses for Blockchain Tracking
    • Investigation Continues While Services Remain Suspended

Mercado Bitcoin Suspends Deposits and Withdrawals

In an official statement on X, Mercado Bitcoin said it had identified and quickly contained a security incident affecting one of its systems. The exchange highlighted two factors: customers were not at a loss for money and data was not leaked.

Comunicado oficial:

Identificamos e contivemos com rapidez um incidente de segurança em um de nossos sistemas nesta madrugada.

Reforçamos que:
• Não houve nenhum prejuízo aos clientes;
• Não houve vazamento de dados.

Como medida preventiva de proteção, depósitos e saques estão temporariamente suspensos. Nossas equipes estão mobilizadas investigando o caso, rastreando os ativos e coordenando as medidas junto às autoridades competentes.

Manteremos atualizações regulares por aqui.

— Mercado Bitcoin (@MercadoBitcoin) November 2, 2026

For a while, no deposits or withdrawals were accepted on the platform as a precaution pending the investigation by the platform’s security teams. The company stated that it was working to identify the hands on the assets and determined the cooperation plan with relevant authorities.

Mercado Bitcoin issued another update indicating that they were still working to safely restore operations to a normal state. It didn’t specify a definite date for the reopening of deposits and withdrawals.

Read More: Binance Says $6.3B Hit in Security Breach, $3B Frozen After DevOps Laptop Compromise

More Than $40 Million in Suspicious Transfers Reportedly Flagged

Its event garnered further excitement when blockchain security outfit Hypernative reportedly spotted over $40 million in suspicious transfers over around 10 blocks.

But it is not advisable to use the reported transaction value as a confirmed theft value. There’s been no public verification that $40 million worth of customer or company assets were stolen by Mercado Bitcoin and no breakdown of the flagged transfers.

The difference matters because unusual on-chain activity could be a sign of security risk, but to be certain of whether it was caused by unauthorized access and what assets were being accessed, an evaluation should be undertaken.

Exchange Publishes Wallet Addresses for Blockchain Tracking

On its sequel announcement, the agency, Mercado Bitcoin, revealed that it had some destination addresses linked to movements investigated. It includes EVM supported blockchains, Bitcoin, Solana, Stellar and TRON.

These addresses were shared only to assist in asset tracking and identification, the exchange said. These are what blockchain monitoring services and other market participants can keep an eye on for additional moves in relation to the identified destinations.

The multi-chain model is applicable as suspicious assets can easily traverse different blockchain networks, complicate the monitoring and/or tracking process.

Investigation Continues While Services Remain Suspended

Mercado Bitcoin has not disclosed any further technical details about the incident, affected systems, or if any wallets of the exchange were compromised.

At this time, a confirmed response was made to contain the incident, suspend all deposits & withdrawals for a while to help protect users, publish tracking addresses, and collaborate with authorities. The amount of $40M is reported but not confirmed as money stolen by the exchange.

Customers are being directed to follow the platform’s official communication channels for updates on the investigation and the restoration of services.

title: Ex-FBI counterintelligence agent stole almost $2.5M in crypto
summary: Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 7, 2026

Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard.

A former FBI counterintelligence agent admitted to wire fraud and money laundering in stealing almost $2.5 million in cryptocurrency from unidentified adversarial nations and wallets that were under investigation.

Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, used his investigative positions with access to FBI systems to steal cryptocurrency, then exchange and launder it through financial transactions to conceal its source and ownership.

Yaroch made about 100 fraudulent transfers related to 35 FBI investigations, gaining $2,474,380.66 in proceeds, according to a news release from the US Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of Virginia on Thursday.

He had earlier admitted to unauthorized transfers that involved about $1 million in digital assets, which was reported by Cointelegraph in August.

Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard, according to the statement.

The former agent admitted that his actions had compromised FBI investigations related to criminal groups and adversarial nations. 

Yaroch faces up to 20 years in prison. His sentencing is set for March 4, 2027.

title: Bitcoin holders have received eCash — What can you do with it?
summary: Bitcoin’s eCash fork gives eligible holders an equivalent balance of ECX, but questions remain over where they can trade the tokens and what they can do with them.
content:
Somewhere between the Binance hack and the US midterms, Paul Sztorc’s long-awaited Bitcoin fork, known as the eCash network, went live.

On Oct. 29, Sztorc, the founder of LayerTwo Labs and the driving force behind the Bitcoin Drivechain proposals BIP300 and BIP301 , launched a separate Bitcoin fork designed to bring payments, privacy and other applications to a network built from Bitcoin’s code.

“We need to actively sabotage the ‘degrowth’ policies killing Bitcoin,” Sztorc tells Magazine.

“We want to find the true Bitcoin builders and give them the tools to actually innovate. We just need the open-minded, risk-taking contrarians to come and build.”

The hard fork gives eligible Bitcoin holders an interesting windfall: their equivalent BTC balance in the new chain’s native token, ECX.

So what benefits does eCash bring to developers, and what can Bitcoin HODLers actually do with their new coins?

What is eCash?

Developed by Sztorc’s LayerTwo Labs, eCash is a separate hard fork of Bitcoin born out of Sztorc’s frustration with some of the “complacency narratives” and “cult-like toxicity” he believes has been holding Bitcoin back.

Sztorc dismisses criticism of Drivechains’ security. Source: archive.ecash

Its main innovation is Drivechains, a system that gives developers freedom to build independent sidechains with different features without having to make changes to Bitcoin’s base-layer protocol (or in this case, eCash’s base layer).

Developers can experiment with different applications for payments, privacy, digital assets and prediction markets, and miners can “maximize their revenues” by earning additional transaction fees.

Five sidechains launched alongside eCash’s mainnet: BitNames, BitAssets, Thunder, Truthcoin and zSide, with two more, the quantum-resistant Photon and decentralized exchange CoinShift, still to come.

Related: Blockchain developer Paul Sztorc announces BTC hard fork eCash

Sztorc has spent over a decade advocating for Drivechains and believes that Bitcoin’s notoriously conservative development approach has held back its potential.

“Anything that isn’t maximizing network usage is simply a distraction,” he says. “Users, the ones who actually pay transaction fees to miners, will win in the long run.”

Getting access to the new coins

The eCash fork took place at Bitcoin block 973,728, and anyone who controlled their private keys at the snapshot received an equivalent ECX balance.

“If you held the keys to your BTC at that exact block, you now own the exact same amount of ECX,” LayerTwo Labs tells Magazine. “It is that simple, and you can access them right now.”

Like beauty, simplicity is in the eye of the beholder, and Bitcoiners who self-custody their coins will need to use a wallet that supports eCash and carefully follow its process to separate the ECX from their BTC.

Because the two networks share transaction history, an unprotected transaction on one chain could be replayed on the other.

eCash Market prices. Source: eCash.

“Never move your BTC first, as an ordinary, unprotected BTC spend can easily be replayed on the ECX network,” LayerTwo Labs warns. Replay controls are built into the protocol, it says, but the company advises holders to move ECX first, before spending BTC.

Anyone keeping BTC on a centralized exchange is “at their mercy regarding distribution,” and should check whether their exchange supports the fork or has announced an ECX distribution.

Where can holders trade ECX?

Accessing ECX isn’t the same thing as being able to sell it and the tokens are not yet widely available on larger crypto exchanges. Depending on which country you are in, there can be tax implications from Bitcoin forks, which are worth looking up before filing your next tax return.

NeoxEX said it opened native ECX deposits, withdrawals and trading on Oct. 29, with ECX/USDT, ECX/USDC and ECX/BTC pairs, while CoinW announced plans to distribute ECX to eligible Bitcoin holders, with deposits, withdrawals and trading to be announced at a later date.

Orca, a decentralized exchange on Solana, lets users swap USDC for wrapped ECX (wECX) through a liquidity pool. That gives holders another way to trade exposure to ECX, but it involves a wrapped token on a different blockchain rather than native ECX trading on the eCash network.

Related: Binance, Polymarket seek Polygon hard fork to recover $6.8M in stolen crypto

How much are the tokens worth? CoinMarketCap placed ECX at $32.63, with around $355,000 in 24-hour trading volume as of Nov. 5, while CoinGecko shows the token as a preview listing, with no price yet available and no tracked exchange markets. Crypto market data provider Kaiko says it does not track ECX, which limits the availability of independent market data.

LayerTwo Labs says early trading saw ECX fluctuate between $40 and $50, but it did not provide supporting order book depth or trading volume figures, pointing instead to the Orca pool’s total value locked as a way for users to assess available liquidity.

eCash is $32.63 on CoinMarketCap as of Nov. 5

“If our fork replicates even a fraction of [Bitcoin Cash] BCH’s initial performance,” Sztorc says, “the liquidity will be staggering,” adding that anyone concerned about low liquidity can hold their coins and decide later.

“We are actively adding new exchanges and trading pairs, so the user experience will only improve,” he says. “Otherwise, you’re welcome to take your free money and leave.”

A different vision for Bitcoin

Sztorc says the value of eCash will ultimately depend on whether developers build useful applications and users are willing to pay for them. Paying customers and transaction fee revenue are the project’s main measures of success during its first year, he says.

He’s not concerned about criticism of Drivechains’ security model, especially the “superstition” that miners could coordinate to steal funds held on sidechains.

“If you genuinely believe miners will torch their own billion-dollar operations for a short-term theft on an L2, then you shouldn’t trust Bitcoin’s L1 either,” he says.

So for now, eCash gives Bitcoiners a new asset and developers a new playground — but whether ECX becomes much more than that will depend on whether anyone actually wants to use it.

title: US sanctions Canadian money-exchange firms over Iran ties
summary: US  also offers as much as $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program.
content:
The US Treasury imposed financial sanctions on eight Canadian money-service companies it claims have done business with sanctioned ‌Iranian entities.

These companies facilitated the exchange of Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets, enabling international transactions, a US Treasury Department statement said on Friday.

The sanctions, which serve to isolate the companies from the dollar-based financial system, are the latest in a series of Treasury moves against firms outside the US.

These businesses have facilitated transactions with sanctioned Iranian digital asset exchanges, as well as with digital asset addresses associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), according to the Treasury.

Bessent says Canada cannot be a safe haven

Related: US plans to seize $1B in crypto linked to Iran this week: Scott Bessent

“Canada cannot be a safe haven for illicit financial facilitators that provide sanctions evasion services to the Iranian regime and its proxies,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Treasury will pursue and disrupt the Iranian regime’s financial channels anywhere in the world.”

Cointelegraph reported in August that the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control, or OFAC, was targeting crypto exchanges facilitating the transfer of funds to Iran’s IRGC. Bessent said at the time that the US planned to “increase the economic pressure” on Iran, focusing on financial networks funding the country’s regime “in dollars, rials, or crypto.”

Friday’s designations are a continuation of Treasury’s campaign to “disrupt the regime’s exploitation of digital assets to fund terrorism, human rights abuses, and attacks on US personnel and allies,” the statement said.

It added that the actions were coordinated with FINTRAC, Canada’s financial intelligence unit.  

Some of the entities subject to this action have changed their names and addresses to evade detection, the statement noted.

Reward of $20 million for Iran nuclear information

In a separate action on Friday, the US Rewards for Justice program offered as much as $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment and personnel.

Iran’s lack of compliance with the International Atomic Energy Agency on safeguards has led to the agency’s loss of “continuity of knowledge” regarding Iran’s production of enriched uranium and components like centrifuges, the statement said.

title: Weekly Review: Prop Firm Match Loses Partners; eToro to Expand in Argentina
summary:
The week brought significant developments across retail
trading, fintech and financial regulation. Prop Firm Match faced a growing
backlash from prop trading firms over its affiliate tracking practices, while
eToro agreed to acquire an Argentine fintech business as it continued expanding
through acq...
content:
The week brought significant developments across retail trading, fintech and financial regulation. Prop Firm Match faced a growing backlash from prop trading firms over its affiliate tracking practices, while eToro agreed to acquire an Argentine fintech business as it continued expanding through acquisitions.

Capital.com also secured a new regulatory licence in Singapore and appointed a former IG executive to lead its local operations.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Regulatory developments included new UK initiatives covering quantum computing and financial crime, alongside changes to transaction reporting requirements. South Africa's regulator also made its withdrawal of Mixirite's licence final.

Meanwhile, artificial intelligence remained a key industry topic, with discussions focusing on how brokers attract customers through AI search and whether investment in the technology can deliver a lasting competitive advantage.

Prop Firm Match Loses Around 21 Partners Over Affiliate Redirect Controversy

Prop Firm Match has lost around 21 prop trading firm partners after acknowledging that clicks on firm profiles and promotional codes opened partner websites through its affiliate links. The exits include Apex Trader Funding, Tradeify, Lucid Trading, Goat Funded Trader, FundingPips and Blue Guardian.

The platform said it disabled the functionality on 29 October and estimated that the potential impact on referral attribution represented a low single-digit percentage of its commissions.

Three years ago, Prop Firm Match launched. Two traders saw a gap in the market for a platform providing simplicity and transparency for prop firm traders. We developed new features not seen before: verified reviews, payout tracking across all payment methods, live spreads, rule overviews, simple ways to compare prop firms, and prop firm expos. Three years in, PFM has had over 25M website visits, reached over 370,000 members, and has given out free challenge accounts worth over $1,400,000 to the PFM community. Over 100 firms apply to be listed each year and go through one of the industry’s most rigorous compliance processes. We also got something wrong. Until yesterday, when someone clicked on a firm or a code on our site, a new tab would open the firm’s site through our affiliate link. This should not have happened. We take full responsibility for it. We have reached out to each of our partners to review this together and reconcile any inaccuracies. We respect any decisions firms have made based on this. We truly appreciate the partners and traders who value the relationship we have built together over the years. We promise you that we will learn from this, hold ourselves to the highest standard, and come back stronger and better.

— Prop Firm Match (@PropFirmMatch) October 31, 2026

However, a source close to the matter said misattributed sales could have appeared as ordinary referrals because tracking cookie periods varied between firms. FundingPips' CEO also said his company had identified the practice in August. The platform has invited current and former partners to review its findings.

eToro Agrees to Acquire Argentine Fintech LB Finanzas

eToro has agreed to acquire Argentine financial app LB Finanzas for an undisclosed amount, marking its fourth acquisition of 2026. The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions and is intended to establish a stronger local presence in Latin America.

LB Finanzas operates an investment platform offering access to equities, cryptocurrencies and payment services. It is regulated by Argentina's National Securities Commission and Central Bank. The acquisition adds local operations and regulatory infrastructure to eToro's regional expansion plans.

Earlier this year, the company agreed to acquire crypto wallet provider Zengo, completed its purchase of Israeli exchange Bit2C and announced an agreement to acquire US brokerage TradeZero, which is expected to close in 2027.

Capital.com Secures Singapore Licence

Capital.com has received a licence from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), allowing its local entity to offer securities, collective investment schemes and over-the-counter derivatives, including contracts for differences (CFDs).

The broker plans to begin onboarding clients in early 2027. It has appointed Tony Lim as Chief Executive of its Singapore operations. Lim previously spent nine years at IG Group's Singapore division as CEO and Managing Director. The appointment follows Capital.com's recent regulatory expansion in South Africa and its recruitment of local executives in Brazil and Chile.

The broker has also been exploring licensing opportunities in markets including Japan and Turkey as it expands its international operations.

FCA Invites Financial Firms to Test Quantum Computing

The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has invited financial firms, quantum computing providers and research institutions to test whether quantum technology can improve money laundering and fraud detection.

Participants will join its new Quantum Experimentation Group and work with an artificial dataset developed by the regulator. The trials will compare quantum machine learning approaches with conventional techniques to address financial crime problems identified by the FCA. Registration closes on 31 December, with the programme scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2027.

The initiative follows the regulator's wider preparations for quantum computing, including a separate warning about the need to adopt encryption capable of withstanding future quantum attacks.

South Africa Makes Mixirite Licence Withdrawal Final

South Africa's Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) has made the withdrawal of Mixirite's financial services licence final, citing material breaches of financial sector laws and failures in client protection.

The decision takes immediate effect after the regulator concluded that the company no longer meets the requirements to operate as a financial services provider. The investigation found that Mixirite's agents used aggressive sales techniques, while unauthorised individuals provided financial advice.

The regulator also identified promises of unrealistic or guaranteed returns, inadequate suitability assessments and governance failures. Mixirite did not oppose the final withdrawal but disputed the findings. Separately, the FSCA expanded its investigation to include four other companies: Complyxpert, Start Stream, Rayn Investments and Advice 365.

Brokers Face New Challenges as AI Chatbots Change Customer Discovery

Artificial intelligence chatbots are changing how retail traders discover and compare brokers, with industry experts warning that strong Google rankings no longer guarantee visibility. Andy Francos, Growth Consultant at Pepperstone, said AI assistants increasingly provide prospective customers with shortlists before they visit individual broker websites.

Wordflow founder Zay Yang highlighted that regulators, comparison platforms and independent media frequently appear ahead of brokers' own websites in AI-generated recommendations. The experts said brokers need accurate, accessible information about licensing, fees and account offerings, preferably presented in plain text rather than scripts or PDFs.

Third-party coverage and credible industry references are also becoming important as AI search engines increasingly determine which brands users consider.

AI Investment Could Raise Costs Without Giving Retail Brokers a Lasting Advantage

Artificial intelligence could help retail brokers improve customer acquisition, automate support and provide more sophisticated trading tools, but the technology may not create a lasting competitive advantage, according to a Finance Magnates analysis by Paul Golden.

Natural language screeners, portfolio analysis and automated execution are among the features changing the trading experience. However, widely available AI models could make these services difficult to differentiate.

Brokers also face integration, monitoring and compliance costs, while increased customer engagement does not necessarily translate into better retention or profitability. The analysis highlights another challenge: as traders increasingly use independent AI agents to compare platforms and execute transactions, brokers could lose control of customer relationships to technology providers.

FCA Revises UK Transaction Reporting Rules

The FCA has finalised changes to the UK's MiFIR transaction reporting framework, aiming to reduce industry costs by more than £100 million annually. The reforms will cut reportable fields from 65 to 52, remove around seven million instruments traded exclusively on EU venues from UK reporting requirements and eliminate duplicate reporting of FX derivatives under MiFIR.

The maximum period for correcting historical reporting errors will also fall from five years to three. The regulator estimates that firms currently spend £493 million annually on transaction reporting. However, implementation will require changes to reporting systems, data management and validation processes.

Quinn Perrott, Co-CEO of TRAction, highlights the operational work firms will need to undertake to adapt to the revised requirements. The new regime will become fully effective on 3 April 2028, although some changes can be adopted earlier.

title: Nigeria Erects Strict Stablecoin Wall, Demanding $11M Local Subsidiaries for US Dollar Tokens

Friday, 06/11/2026 | 21:54 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Dollar stablecoins can serve Nigerian retail users only through a locally incorporated, CBN-licensed issuer.
  • Stablecoin payments or remittances might require separate CBN approval.

Nigeria has adopted regulations for non-security virtual assets that make it one of the most restrictive stablecoin market-access regimes currently in force.

According to the document, published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), foreign issuers must build a locally licensed operation before making their tokens available to retail customers. New rules combine local incorporation, token-level approval, capital requirements and separate permissions for payment functions.

The regulations, effective from 5 November, apply to overseas companies targeting Nigerian users even when those businesses have no physical presence in the country.

Dollar Stablecoins Need a Nigerian Issuer

The CBN divides stablecoins into two categories. Class 1 covers tokens pegged to the naira, while Class 2 applies to those referencing foreign currencies, such as dollar-backed tokens USDT or USDC.

Foreign issuers are effectively cut off from the local retail customers until they establish a Nigerian company, obtain Class 2 issuer licence, and CBN approval for their tokens

That local company must maintain at least NGN15 billion (approximately $11.1 million) in paid-up capital and provide operational liquidity for redemptions in Nigeria.

Tokens must be fully backed by assets denominated in their reference currency, with an additional 2% buffer. The issuer must also appoint a Nigerian bank to process local redemption requests.

Stablecoin Payments Require a Second Approval

The new framework divides oversight: the SEC remains responsible for trading and investment-related custody, while the CBN controls payment and money-transfer services.

An SEC-licensed crypto platform can therefore list a stablecoin or hold it for trading clients. However, for customer transfers, merchant payments, remittances, payment gateways or stored-value products separate CBN authorisation is required.

These permissions are activity-specific. A company authorised for custody or exchange cannot assume that the same approval covers a P2P service or cross-border payments.

Providers of these non-issuance services must also maintain at least NGN1 billion, or approximately $741,000, in additional capital. Moreover, a SEC-regulated platform cannot use the same funds to satisfy both regulators’ requirements.

Conversions between naira and a foreign-currency stablecoin may require an authorised foreign-exchange channel, transaction reporting and specific CBN approval.

This regulatory approach creates a layered model in which the token, its issuer and each payment function must all receive the appropriate permission.

Nigeria Is Already One of Africa’s Largest Crypto Markets

The rules apply to a market where cryptoassets are used for more than speculative trading. Stablecoins provide Nigerian citizens and businesses with access to dollar-denominated value and an alternative channel for cross-border payments when conventional transfers are expensive or foreign currency is difficult to obtain.

Chainalysis estimated that Nigeria recorded $38.1 billion in crypto activity between July 2025 and June 2026, slightly below South Africa’s $39.3 billion. Nigeria also ranked third in the company’s global grassroots adoption index, which measures patterns of everyday use rather than absolute transaction volume.

Stablecoin activity through peer-to-peer channels increased more than sixfold between 2022 and 2026, from $2.3 billion to $14.6 billion, according to the same study. This combination of dollar demand, cross-border use and growing domestic distribution helps explain the structure of the CBN regime.

The regulator is permitting stablecoins, but wants their issuance, conversion and payment functions to pass through locally supervised companies and approved financial channels.

Existing operators have 180 days to apply, but may continue only at their current scale during the transition. They must register within 30 days and begin supervisory reporting within 60 days, making expansion dependent on securing the new approvals.

    Tradeview Markets EDGE: How AI Is Changing Trade Execution | Timothy Furey

    Can artificial intelligence improve the way brokers execute trades? In this exclusive interview from iFX EXPO Asia 2026 in Hong Kong, Neophytos Papageorgiou, CEO of Finance Magnates, speaks with Timothy Furey, Founder and CEO of Tradeview Markets, about the company's proprietary execution technology and its approach to liquidity management. title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
FinCEN issued a final order under section 9714(a) that will bar U.S. financial institutions from sending or receiving funds with MEXC Global 30 days after Federal Register publication, ...
content:
The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said.

FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC.

Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking.

Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says.

What the order does — and when

The order, signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations.

Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending.

Background on MEXC

Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions.

Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission warned the same month that the platform was marketing to local investors without a licence. Seychelles’ Financial Services Authority said in May 2026 it took action against MX Global Ltd for unlicensed virtual-asset operations — footnoted in FinCEN’s order.

Those compliance gaps matter because the illicit-flow thesis is specific, not guilt by association. Beyond Russia, FinCEN cites about $1 billion in direct traffic with more than 40 Iranian crypto exchangers, nearly $26 million with the OFAC-sanctioned A7 sanctions-evasion network, and almost $200 million tied to the A7A5 stablecoin. DPRK facilitators and cybercrime flows are also alleged. MEXC has not issued a public response to the Friday order; its main X account kept posting marketing content through the afternoon.

Why it matters for bitcoin markets

Practically, once the order bites, U.S. banks, money transmitters and other covered firms cannot move dollars or crypto to MEXC wallets or accounts. Offshore users may keep trading peer-to-peer, but dollar on-ramps and any bank that still clears for MEXC become legal risk. The template tracks earlier 9714 cut-offs of venues such as Bitzlato, and it lands beside a busy sanctions week that has already seen North Korea crypto designations, an Iranian exchange action, and Russia’s push to put bitcoin trading on the Moscow Exchange.

Whether MEXC contests the finding, seeks an exemption, or quietly reroutes liquidity is the open question. For now the paper trail is clear: a final FinCEN order under 9714(a), a 30-day fuse after Federal Register publication, and Treasury’s claim of at least $16 billion in illicit volume sitting behind the cut-off.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Finance Magnates Awards 2026 Winners Announced
summary: Finance Magnates has announced the winners of the Finance Magnates Awards 2026, recognising leading companies and CEOs across online trading, fintech, payments and financial services. The awards honour firms across global, regional and national markets, alongside two CEOs named CEO of the Year 2026 ...
content:
Finance Magnates has announced the winners of the Finance Magnates Awards 2026, recognising leading companies and CEOs across online trading, fintech, payments and financial services. The awards honour firms across global, regional and national markets, alongside two CEOs named CEO of the Year 2026 in the B2C and B2B categories.

The winners were announced at the Finance Magnates Awards Gala Dinner & Ceremony in Limassol, Cyprus on November 6, 2026, bringing together companies and professionals from across the financial industry for an evening of recognition.

The Finance Magnates Awards recognise firms across a wide range of categories, including brokerage services, proprietary trading, institutional trading, payments, financial technology and services for brokers.

The 2026 awards feature winners across Global, Regional and National categories for Brokerage (B2C), alongside dedicated awards for Fintech (B2B) firms operating in Institutional Trading, Services for Brokers and Tech for Brokers.

Finance Magnates Awards 2026: Brokerage (B2C) Winners

The Brokerage (B2C) awards recognise companies serving traders and investors across global markets. The winners span brokerage firms and proprietary trading businesses, with awards covering areas such as innovation, customer service, trading conditions and overall performance.

Global Award Winners

The Global categories recognise companies operating across international markets.

  • Most Established Broker 2026: Tickmill

  • Best Rising Star Broker 2026: IQ Broker

  • Most Innovative Broker 2026: FXT

  • Most Trusted Broker 2026: TradingPRO

  • Best Overall Broker 2026: Fotmarkets

  • Most Transparent Broker 2026: RoboMarkets

  • Best Multi-Asset Prop Trading Firm 2026: FundedNext

  • Most Established Prop Firm 2026: FundingPips

  • Best Trading Environment 2026: Elev8

Regional Award Winners

The Regional awards recognise companies across key financial markets, including MENA, LATAM, Asia, Africa and Europe.

  • Most Established Broker 2026 (MENA): CFI Financial Group

  • Best Trading Conditions 2026 (LATAM): HFM

  • Most Trusted Broker 2026 (MENA): TMGM

  • Best Rising Broker 2026 (Asia): Octrado

  • Most Disruptive Broker 2026 (MENA): Base Markets

  • Most Customer-Focused Broker 2026 (Asia): TradingPRO

  • Broker of the Year 2026 (Africa): Headway

  • Best Trading Conditions 2026 (EU): TMGM

  • Most Innovative Prop Trading Firm 2026 (EU): AIFO

  • Most Accessible Trading Platform 2026 (MENA): Olymptrade

National Award Winners

The National categories recognise companies for their work in specific markets.

  • Most Innovative Trading Platform 2026 (Colombia): LBX

  • Most Innovative Broker 2026 (UAE): CFI Financial Group

  • Most Transparent Broker 2026 (Indonesia): TradingPRO

  • Broker of the Year 2026 (Indonesia): Headway

  • Best Emerging Prop Firm 2026 (Japan): Fundora

  • Best Futures Market Analysis Platform 2026 (USA): Bookmap

  • Broker of the Year 2026 (Malaysia): Headway

  • Best Trading Conditions 2026 (Germany): RoboMarkets

  • Best Customer Support Experience 2026 (Philippines): Olymptrade

Finance Magnates Awards 2026: Fintech (B2B) Winners

The Fintech (B2B) awards recognise companies providing services, technology and infrastructure to the financial industry.

The awards cover three main groups: Institutional Trading, Services for Brokers and Tech for Brokers.

Institutional Trading Award Winners

The Institutional Trading categories recognise firms providing services and solutions for institutional market participants.

  • Best Multi-Asset Investment Provider 2026: Freedom24

  • Best Real-Time Risk Management Solution 2026: iSAM Securities

  • Best Liquidity Provider 2026: Exinity Connect

  • Best Trading Infrastructure Provider 2026: FinPrime Group

Services for Brokers Award Winners

The Services for Brokers categories recognise companies supporting brokerage businesses through regulatory, licensing and payment services.

  • Best Regulatory & Licensing Partner 2026: FiveComply

  • Best Africa Payments Infrastructure 2026: Kora

Tech for Brokers Award Winners

The Tech for Brokers categories recognise technology firms supporting brokers through trading tools, infrastructure, risk management and payment solutions.

  • Best Bridge Provider 2026: Centroid Solutions

  • Best Technology Provider 2026: FYNXT

  • Best Brokerage Services Provider 2026: Freedom24

  • Best Enterprise Prop Trading Infrastructure 2026: Axcera

  • Best Risk Management Technology Provider 2026: TapaaS

  • Best Crypto Payments Technology for Brokers 2026: Overchain

Finance Magnates CEO of the Year 2026 Winners

The Finance Magnates Awards 2026 also recognised two business leaders for their contributions to the financial industry, naming separate winners in the B2C and B2B categories.

CEO of the Year 2026 – B2C: Ziad Melhem, CFI Financial Group

Ziad Melhem, CEO of CFI Financial Group, was named CEO of the Year 2026 (B2C).

Melhem leads the Group’s global strategy, operational performance and expansion across MENA and key international markets. Previously CFI’s Group Chief Marketing Officer, he brings extensive experience across finance, technology and business development, with a focus on long-term value creation, client trust and sustainable growth.

Read his full bio on the CFI Financial Group website.

CEO of the Year 2026 – B2B: Cristian Vlasceanu, Centroid Solutions

Cristian Vlasceanu, CEO of Centroid Solutions, was named CEO of the Year 2026 (B2B).

Recognised for his expertise in financial technology, Vlasceanu rose through software engineering roles to lead Centroid Solutions as CEO. He oversees the company’s team, supports its clients and drives product improvement.

Under his leadership, Centroid Solutions established its One-Centroid Ecosystem, expanding its offering to include a multi-asset trading platform and CLM/CRM alongside its core connectivity bridge, risk engine and network infrastructure solutions.

Recognising Achievement Across the Financial Industry

The Finance Magnates Awards recognise brands and leaders across the financial sector, from online trading and prop trading services to fintech, payments and institutional trading.

By covering both B2C and B2B categories, the awards highlight companies serving traders and investors, as well as those providing the technology, services and infrastructure that support financial businesses.

Finance Magnates congratulates all the winners of the 2026 Awards and thanks the companies, industry professionals, voters and judges who took part.

For more information, visit Finance Magnates Awards Winners.

MEXC will refer eligible French customers to Kraken, extending a transition arrangement the two crypto exchanges previously used in the Netherlands.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The Kraken announcement follows MEXC’s October 28 notice that it would gradually stop serving users linked to France. MEXC attributed the decision to regulatory alignment.

The referral does not automatically move customer accounts, balances or trading positions, according to the announcement. French users choosing Kraken will need to open a separate account, complete KYC procedures and transfer their assets themselves.

Kraken’s crypto services in France are provided by Payward Europe Solutions Limited, which is authorised under MiCA in Ireland and listed by the AMF as permitted to serve French clients.

Trading Restrictions Begin in November

MEXC has divided affected customers into four groups based on their account and identity verification information. The first group enters the wind-down process on November 18, 2026, followed by others on December 10, December 31 and January 22, 2027.

Once an account enters wind-down mode, the customer cannot open or increase positions, make new spot purchases or deposit additional funds. Existing positions can still be reduced or closed, liabilities repaid and assets withdrawn.

MEXC plans to close any remaining positions automatically at 00:00 on January 22, 2027. For customers in the fourth group, that is also when wind-down restrictions begin, so they must close positions by January 21 to avoid automatic closure.

All affected accounts move to withdrawal-only status on January 25. Withdrawals through MEXC close at 00:00 on March 5, 2027, rather than remaining available throughout that day.

France Extends an Earlier EU Exit

MEXC previously stopped serving customers in the Netherlands and recommended regulated alternatives, including Kraken and Bybit EU. Customers who chose another exchange had to open a new account; their MEXC accounts were not migrated.

The French withdrawal also follows an earlier regulatory warning. The AMF added www.mexc.com to its blacklist on June 4, 2024, and included the platform in a public warning the following day about websites offering digital-asset services without the required authorisation.

MEXC has named Kraken as the custodian for assets left by Dutch customers after offboarding, a separate arrangement that does not require them to open a Kraken account.

For France, MEXC says assets remaining after the withdrawal deadline will go to a regulated custodian, but it has not identified the company or explained how customers will later claim those holdings.

title: Warsaw Stock Exchange Taps XTB to Bring Foreign Retail Investors to Polish Stocks
summary:
Warsaw-listed shares are now open to XTB S.A.'s clients across the European Union without a separate request, the broker and the Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW) said today (Friday). The two called it a pilot.
Until October, only XTB clients in Poland had automatic access to Warsaw-listed instruments on ...
content:
2026-11-06T21:10:38.310+02:00

Friday, 06/11/2026 | 19:10 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • EU clients of the broker can now buy Warsaw-listed shares without the extra application needed until October.
  • Domestic brokerage accounts topped 3 million in September, and 1.285 million of them sit at XTB.

Warsaw-listed shares are now open to XTB S.A.'s clients across the European Union without a separate request, the broker and the Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW) said today (Friday). The two called it a pilot.

Until October, only XTB clients in Poland had automatic access to Warsaw-listed instruments on its platform. Retail investors elsewhere needed an extra application first.

That route was used by clients in France, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, the UK, Portugal, Romania and Spain, according to the release.

The exchange 's retail growth has so far been counted in domestic accounts. The Central Securities Depository of Poland (KDPW) counted more than 3 million brokerage accounts at the end of September, 1.285 million of them at XTB, up from 2,856,520 accounts in May, FM Intelligence data show.

London's trading industry is coming home!

A Polish Firm With a Foreign Client Base

XTB brings the exchange a client base already split between Poland and abroad. Poland generated 54.4% of XTB's 2025 revenue, as FinanceMagnates.com reported when Lynx opened a Warsaw office to compete for Polish savers.

XTB says more than 3.2 million people use its investing app. FM Intelligence's FX/CFD heat map shows by country where web traffic to XTB and 97 other retail brokers comes from.

One of its biggest sources of new accounts lies outside the bloc the pilot covers first: Indonesia now trails only Poland by new accounts, XTB Chief Executive Omar Arnaout said last week.

Filip Kaczmarzyk, a member of XTB's management board, said demand for Polish shares already comes from outside the country.

"We also see interest in the Polish market from our foreign clients," Kaczmarzyk said, adding that automatic access removes operational barriers for investors abroad.

He named CD Projekt, Benefit Systems and LPP as examples of Warsaw-listed companies with business in many international markets.

Index Gains Give the Exchange a Pitch

The cooperation runs under a GPW program aimed at exchange members that serve foreign retail investors. XTB will also run information and promotional campaigns about the Polish market, a month after it launched what it calls the biggest ad campaign in its history.

"We want to use their international reach," said Michał Kobza, a member of the Warsaw Stock Exchange's management board, referring to the brokers in the program.

Kobza said a larger share of foreign investors would support liquidity and make Warsaw-listed companies better known abroad.

The exchange pointed to this year's returns. The WIG20 index has risen more than 34% since January and the mWIG40 30%, against less than 13% for the S&P 500 over the same period.

XTB has been listed on the Warsaw exchange since 2016, and last week reported that its third-quarter profit quadrupled from a year earlier. The two gave no date for clients outside the EU.

title: Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary
Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign for Aaron van Wirdum's The Genesis Book, capping a hand-signed Collectors Edition at 333 numbered copies.
This post Bitcoin Magazine B...
content:
Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book, offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase.

Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package.

Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package.

Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced.

What ships with the anniversary editions

Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files.

A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar.

Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027.

Van Wirdum, who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work.

Store images for the slipcase and accessories are artistic renderings; the campaign page notes that color, materials and finishes may vary in production. The campaign is operated by BTC Inc., which publishes Bitcoin Magazine.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Coinhub Brand Enters Simulated Prop Trading Through Nevis Firm
summary:
Coinhub Funded has launched a simulated proprietary trading programme that combines evaluations and instant funding with up to nine short weekday trading tournaments. 
Coinhub Is Not the Prop-Firm Operator 
The launch announcement connects the new business with Coinhub’s network of more than 2,000 B...
content:
2026-11-06T20:18:00.000+02:00

Friday, 06/11/2026 | 18:18 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • A Nevis company has launched Coinhub-branded prop accounts that pay traders for simulated results.
  • Separate USDT tournaments run alongside the programme, but winning one does not qualify a trader for a funded account.

Coinhub Funded has launched a simulated proprietary trading programme that combines evaluations and instant funding with up to nine short weekday trading tournaments.

Coinhub Is Not the Prop-Firm Operator

The launch announcement connects the new business with Coinhub’s network of more than 2,000 Bitcoin ATMs across the United States. However, the network and the prop firm have different operators.

The ATM network is operated by Nevada-based LSGT Services LLC under the Coinhub trade name. Coinhub Funded’s client agreement instead names Block Entertainment Operating LLC, a company registered in Nevis.

According to the launch announcement, the prop firm uses the Coinhub name and logo under an intellectual property licensing agreement.

Funded Accounts Run on Simulated Trades

Under the prop firm’s terms, both evaluations and funded accounts operate in a demo environment. No trades reach the real market, and traders do not manage the operator’s capital.

The company describes payouts as performance-based commissions calculated from simulated results and says it does not operate as a broker, dealer or investment adviser.

Traders enter the funded programme by purchasing a one- or two-step evaluation and meeting its targets on a simulated account. They can skip that stage by buying an Instant Funding account, but the faster track has tighter risk limits and a lower ceiling: $25,000 in virtual capital, compared with $200,000 on the two-step programme.

Traders may hold several accounts, provided their combined starting allocation does not exceed $500,000. Both routes use the same simulated platform for crypto, forex, indices, metals and commodities.

Traders Receive Payouts in USDT

Payments depend on the results recorded there, not on the advertised account size. The standard commission is 80% of qualifying simulated profits.

Traders who pass an evaluation can raise their share to 90% by purchasing an add-on; Instant Funding keeps the 80% rate. Eligible traders can request payouts at 14-day intervals, in USDT or cash at cash-enabled Coinhub ATMs.

Each account also has a lifetime payout limit equal to its starting virtual balance and closes once that limit is reached.

Coinhub Funded also schedules up to nine short simulated tournaments on weekdays. Some have paid entry and USDT prizes, but winning a tournament does not qualify a trader for a funded account; that remains a separate programme accessed through an evaluation or Instant Funding.

title: Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block
Thailand's SEC filed a criminal complaint against Bitget operator BG Limited for unlicensed Thai trading from 2022 to 2025.
This post Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec....
content:
Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5.

The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026.

From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok.

That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts.

Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff.

A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case

The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd.

Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules.

“Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release.

The timetable has already slipped. GMO Internet Group pushed the effective date of the share transfer from Oct. 31 to Nov. 30, citing careful work on Thai regulatory applications and closing procedures. That revised date sits five days before the planned Bitget access block.

CoinDesk reported that Bitget’s own terms of use, updated in October, already list Thailand among jurisdictions where its services are prohibited, and that the SEC has not said whether the criminal complaint will weigh on the GMO-Z change of control.

What the block does and does not settle

Thailand has used the same access-blocking tool before. In mid-2025 the SEC referred Bybit, OKX and three other unlicensed platforms for a June 28 cutoff, telling users to move assets first. The Bitget action follows that template — and adds a criminal complaint against the exchange operator and a named promoter.

Licensed venues still sit at the center of Bangkok’s policy mix. Thailand has approved a multi-year capital-gains tax break only for trades on SEC-regulated platforms, and has been expanding regulated crypto products in derivatives and capital markets. Unlicensed platforms get the opposite treatment: investor alerts, access blocks and, now for Bitget, a police referral.

What is not yet clear is whether a criminal case against BG Limited for the 2022–2025 period bars, slows or leaves untouched BTGT’s bid to take over a licensed local operator. The SEC statement does not mention GMO-Z. Bitget has not publicly answered the complaint in a statement posted with the acquisition release.

For Thai users still on Bitget, the practical clock is Dec. 5. For Bitget, the test is whether Nov. 30 closes a regulated door into Thailand — or whether the complaint filed Thursday makes that licensed path the next question the ECD and the SEC have to answer.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations
Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, pleaded guilty Thursday to wire fraud and money laundering after using wallet credentials from 35 FBI investigations to take about $2.47 million i...
content:
A former FBI agent pleaded guilty Thursday to stealing about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency with wallet credentials the bureau had collected in its own cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia announced.

Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027.

Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. Prosecutors say Yaroch made roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using credentials tied to 35 separate FBI investigations, drawing on wallets controlled by investigation subjects, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI itself had created for an operation.

The Justice Department Office of the Inspector General had flagged the case in August after Yaroch’s arrest on a criminal complaint. That earlier account described a smaller set of transfers — about 10 moves totaling roughly $1 million — and noted that Yaroch self-reported the activity to two department employees on July 29, 2026. The plea figures are larger.

From 2017 through early 2025, Yaroch worked in the FBI Boston Division on a squad focused on an adversarial nation-state. From February 2025 through July 31, 2026, he served in the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division at headquarters, with access to systems that stored cryptocurrency credentials gathered in investigations.

How the FBI credentials turned into cash

Beginning no later than December 2024, Yaroch used that access to move coins out of those wallets and into ones he controlled. After the transfers, he swapped the stolen cryptocurrency into other digital assets and ran further transactions meant to obscure its source, nature and ownership.

Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts, then shuffled funds among other accounts to cover debts, including credit cards, car payments and loans, the office said.

FOX 5 DC, citing the same U.S. Attorney’s Office release, noted the Portugal planning that appears in the plea papers. Yaroch asked ChatGPT how to maximize investment returns and where to live in the European Union. After the chatbot suggested buying a vineyard in Portugal, he gave Portuguese lawyers a power of attorney on June 15, 2026, to register him with the Portuguese Tax and Customs Authority, obtain a tax identification number and collect the password to his finance portal. He arranged travel to Portugal for September 2026.

What the plea says the FBI lost

The agreed statement of facts goes beyond the dollar figure. Yaroch’s conduct compromised multiple FBI investigations into criminal groups and nation-state adversaries, the office said, and it compromised FBI sources and methods used in foreign intelligence collection and criminal cases. It also “deprived FBI employees of their ability to carry out their functions to protect public safety and national security.”

First Assistant U.S. Attorney Theophani K. Stamos and Daniel S. Wierzbicki, special agent in charge of the FBI Washington Field Office’s Counterintelligence Division, announced the plea. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kathleen Robeson and Russell Carlberg are prosecuting, with help from the National Security Cyber Section of the Justice Department’s National Security Division and the DOJ inspector general’s Mid-Atlantic region. The case is 1:26-CR-208 in the Eastern District of Virginia.

The admission lands in a week when federal crypto-crime stories keep stacking up — from a failed bitcoin kidnapping plot that produced its own guilty plea last month to FBI tallies putting U.S. crypto fraud losses above $11 billion in 2025, a figure the White House has used to frame a wider crackdown.

What sentencing will do with the gap between Yaroch’s July self-report and the $2.47 million plea figure is still open. So is how many of the 35 FBI cases can be repaired after an insider treated the bureau’s own wallet credentials as a personal ATM. March 4, 2027, is when Judge Giles gets to answer the first question.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.
